title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第三十六: 尒朱榮
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第三十六: 尒朱榮 Volume 48 Biographies 36: Er Zhurong

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮 子文暢 文略 從子兆 從弟彥伯 彥伯子敞 彥伯弟仲遠 世隆 榮從父弟度律 榮從祖兄子天光

translations.literal: Er Zhurong; his sons Wenchang and Wenlue; his nephew Zhao; his cousin Yanbo; Yanbo's son Chang; Yanbo's brother Zhongyuan; Shilong; Rong's uncle's younger brother Dulü; Rong's elder cousin's son Tiangguang
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong; his sons Wenchang and Wenlue; his nephew Zhao; his cousin Yanbo; Yanbo's son Chang; Yanbo's brother Zhongyuan; Shilong; Rong's uncle's younger brother Dulü; Rong's elder cousin's son Tiangguang

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮

translations.literal: Er Zhurong
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮，字天寶，北秀容人也。

translations.literal: Er Zhurong, styled Tianbao, was a native of Northern Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong, styled Tianbao, was a native of Northern Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 世為部落酋帥，其先居尒硃川，因為氏焉。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; their ancestors dwelt in Erzhu River and took it as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; their ancestors dwelt in Erzhu River and took it as their surname.

sentences.zh: 高祖羽健，魏登國初為領人酋長，率契胡武士從平晉陽，定中山，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu Jian, at the beginning of Wei's Dengguo reign, served as chief of the leading clan and led Qi-hu warriors in pacifying Jinyang and settling Zhongshan, and was appointed Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu Jian, at the beginning of Wei's Dengguo reign, served as chief of the leading clan and led Qi-hu warriors in pacifying Jinyang and settling Zhongshan, and was appointed Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以居秀容川，詔割方三百里封之，長為世業。

translations.literal: Because he dwelt at Xiurong River, an edict carved out three hundred square li and enfeoffed it to him, to be held in perpetuity as hereditary domain.
translations.idiomatic: Because he dwelt at Xiurong River, an edict carved out three hundred square li and enfeoffed it to him as a hereditary domain held in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 道武初，以南秀容川原沃衍，欲令居之。

translations.literal: In the early Daowu era, because Southern Xiurong River's plains were fertile and broad, the court wished to have him relocate there.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Daowu era, because Southern Xiurong River's plains were fertile and broad, the court wished to have him relocate there.

sentences.zh: 羽健曰：「家世奉國，給侍左右，北秀容既在髂內，差近京師，豈以沃鹆脊，更遷遠地？

translations.literal: Yu Jian said: "Our family has served the state for generations, attending at court. Northern Xiurong is within the inner frontier and comparatively near the capital—how could we exchange fertile land for a more distant posting?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian said: "Our family has served the state for generations, attending at court. Northern Xiurong lies within the inner frontier and is comparatively near the capital—how could we exchange fertile land for a more distant posting?

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 所居處曾有狗舐地，因而穿之得甘泉，因名狗舐泉。

translations.literal: At the place where he dwelt, a dog once licked the ground; digging there they found a sweet spring, hence it was named Dog-Lick Spring.
translations.idiomatic: At the place where he dwelt, a dog once licked the ground. Digging there, they found a sweet spring, hence the name Dog-Lick Spring.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鬱德、祖代勤，繼為酋長。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Yude and grandfather Daiqin successively served as chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Yude and grandfather Daiqin successively served as chiefs.

sentences.zh: 代勤，太武敬哀皇后舅也。

translations.literal: Daiqin was maternal uncle to Emperor Taiwu's Respected and Lamented Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Daiqin was maternal uncle to Emperor Taiwu's Respected and Lamented Empress.

sentences.zh: 既以外親，兼數征伐有功，給復百年，除立義將軍。

translations.literal: Because of this royal connection, and having repeatedly achieved merit in campaigns, he was granted a hundred-year exemption from tax and labor service and was appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this royal connection, and having repeatedly achieved merit in campaigns, he was granted a hundred-year exemption from tax and labor service and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 曾圍山而獵，部人射虎，誤中其髀。

translations.literal: Once while hunting on the mountains, a tribesman shot at a tiger and accidentally hit Daiqin in the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting in the mountains, a tribesman shot at a tiger and accidentally hit Daiqin in the thigh.

sentences.zh: 代勤仍令拔箭，竟不推問，曰：「此既過誤，何忍加罪。

translations.literal: Daiqin still had the arrow pulled out and never pursued the inquiry, saying: "This was an accident—how could I bear to punish him?
translations.idiomatic: Daiqin still had the arrow pulled out and never pursued the inquiry, saying: "This was an accident—how could I bear to punish him?

sentences.zh: 」部內咸感其意。

translations.literal: " All within his domain were moved by his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: " All within his domain were moved by his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 位肆州刺史，封梁郡公，以老致仕，歲賜帛百疋以為常。

translations.literal: He rose to Inspector of Sizhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery; in old age he retired and was annually granted a hundred bolts of silk as a fixed stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Inspector of Sizhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang Commandery. In old age he retired and was annually granted a hundred bolts of silk as a fixed stipend.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，追贈太師、司徒公、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Steward, and Director of the Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Steward, and Director of the Masters of Writing Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父新興，太和中繼為酋長。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing, in the Taihe era succeeded as chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing succeeded as chief in the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 曾行馬群，見一白蛇，頭有兩角，咒之，求畜牧蕃息。

translations.literal: Once while tending the horse herds he saw a white serpent with two horns; he prayed over it, seeking that livestock breed and multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Once while tending the horse herds he saw a white serpent with two horns. He prayed over it, seeking that his livestock breed and multiply.

sentences.zh: 自是牛羊駝馬，日覺滋盛，色別為群，穀量之。

translations.literal: From then on cattle, sheep, camels, and horses daily grew more plentiful, sorted by color into separate herds and counted by grain measures.
translations.idiomatic: From then on cattle, sheep, camels, and horses daily grew more plentiful, sorted by color into separate herds and counted by grain measures.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有征討，輒獻私馬，兼備資糧，助裨軍用。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had campaigns, he would present his private horses and supply provisions, assisting the military effort.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court mounted campaigns, he presented his private horses and supplied provisions to assist the military effort.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was pleased with this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was pleased with this.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛，特聽冬朝京師，夏歸部落。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was specially permitted to come to court in winter and return to his tribe in summer.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was specially permitted to come to court in winter and return to his tribe in summer.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，諸公王朝貴，競以珍玩遺之，新興亦報以名馬。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered court, princes, dukes, and grandees competed to present him with rare treasures, and Xinxing reciprocated with famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court, princes, dukes, and grandees competed to present him with rare treasures, and Xinxing reciprocated with famous horses.

sentences.zh: 位散騎常侍、平北將軍、秀容第一領人酋長。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Chief of the First Leading Clan of Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Chief of the First Leading Clan of Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 新興每春秋二時，恆與妻子閱畜牧于川澤，射獵自娛。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would invariably review the livestock with his wife and children in the rivers and marshes, hunting for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would review the livestock with his wife and children in the rivers and marshes, hunting for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，以年老，啟求傳爵于榮。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, citing old age, he petitioned to transmit his enfeoffment to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's time, citing old age, he petitioned to transmit his enfeoffment to Rong.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously named Jian.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，贈太師、相國、西河郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and Prince of Xihe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and Prince of Xihe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 榮潔白，美容貌，幼而神機明決。

translations.literal: Rong was fair-complexioned and handsome in appearance, sharp and decisive even as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was fair-complexioned and handsome, sharp and decisive even as a child.

sentences.zh: 及長，好射獵，每設圍誓眾，便為軍陣之法，號令嚴肅，眾莫敢犯。

translations.literal: When grown he loved hunting and shooting; whenever he organized a hunt and gathered the crowd, he arrayed them in military formations with stern commands that none dared violate.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he loved hunting and shooting. Whenever he organized a hunt and gathered the crowd, he arrayed them in military formations with stern commands that none dared violate.

sentences.zh: 秀容界有池三所，在高山上，清深不測，相傳曰祁連池，魏言天池也。

translations.literal: Within Xiurong's borders were three pools on high mountains, deep and unfathomably clear; tradition held they were the Qilian Pools, called in Wei speech the Heavenly Pools.
translations.idiomatic: Within Xiurong's borders were three pools on high mountains, deep and unfathomably clear. Tradition held they were the Qilian Pools, called in Wei speech the Heavenly Pools.

sentences.zh: 父新興曾與榮游池上，忽聞簫鼓音，謂榮曰：「古老相傳，聞此聲，皆至公輔。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing once went sightseeing at the pool with Rong and suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums; he said to Rong: "Ancient tradition holds that whoever hears this sound will reach the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing once went sightseeing at the pool with Rong and suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums. He said to Rong: "Ancient tradition holds that whoever hears this sound will reach the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 吾年老暮，當為汝耳。

translations.literal: I am old and in my twilight years—it will be for you.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and in my twilight years—it will be for you.

sentences.zh: 」榮襲爵，後除直寢、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: " Rong inherited the enfeoffment and was later appointed Direct Attendant and General Who Attacks at Large.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong inherited the enfeoffment and was later appointed Direct Attendant and General Who Attacks at Large.

sentences.zh: 正光中，四方兵起，遂散畜牧，招合義勇。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, when rebellion broke out on all sides, he dispersed his herds and recruited righteous volunteers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era, when rebellion broke out on all sides, he dispersed his herds and recruited righteous volunteers.

sentences.zh: 以討賊功，進封博陵郡公，其梁郡前爵聽賜第二子。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing bandits, he was advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery; the prior title of Duke of Liang was granted to his second son.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in suppressing bandits, he was advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery, and the prior title of Duke of Liang was granted to his second son.

sentences.zh: 時榮率眾至肆州，刺史尉慶賓閉城不納。

translations.literal: At that time Rong led his forces to Sizhou; Inspector Wei Qingbin closed the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Rong led his forces to Sizhou, but Inspector Wei Qingbin closed the gates and would not admit them.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，攻拔之，乃署其從叔羽生為刺史，執慶賓還秀容。

translations.literal: Rong was enraged, stormed and took the city, appointed his uncle-by-clan Yusheng as inspector, and took Qingbin back to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was enraged, stormed and took the city, appointed his uncle-by-clan Yusheng as inspector, and took Qingbin back to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 自是兵威漸盛，朝廷亦不能罪責。

translations.literal: From then his military might gradually grew, and the court could not punish or blame him.
translations.idiomatic: From then his military might gradually grew, and the court could not punish or blame him.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮吞杜洛周，榮恐其南逼鄴城，表求東援相州，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong swallowed Du Luozhou, Rong feared he would press south toward Ye and memorialized requesting eastern aid for Xiangzhou; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong swallowed Du Luozhou, Rong feared he would press south toward Ye and memorialized requesting eastern aid for Xiangzhou, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 榮以山東賊盛，慮其西逸，乃遣兵固守滏口以防之。

translations.literal: Rong, because bandits in the east were powerful and he feared their westward flight, sent troops to hold Fuyu Pass against them.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandits in the east were powerful and he feared their westward flight, Rong sent troops to hold Fuyu Pass against them.

sentences.zh: 於是北捍馬邑，東塞井陘。

translations.literal: Thus he defended Mayi in the north and blocked Jingxing Pass in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he defended Mayi in the north and blocked Jingxing Pass in the east.

sentences.zh: 尋屬明帝崩，事出倉卒，榮乃與元天穆等密議，入匡朝廷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Ming died; the matter arose in sudden haste, and Rong secretly deliberated with Yuan Tianmu and others on entering to restore the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Ming died. The matter arose in sudden haste, and Rong secretly deliberated with Yuan Tianmu and others on marching in to restore the court.

sentences.zh: 抗表云：「今海內草草，異口一言，皆云大行皇帝鴆毒致禍，舉潘嬪之女以誑百姓，奉未言之兒而臨四海。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating: "The realm is now in turmoil—every mouth speaks as one, saying the late emperor met disaster through poisoning, that the daughter of Lady Pan is held up to deceive the people, and an infant who cannot yet speak is set to rule the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating: "The realm is in turmoil—every mouth speaks as one, saying the late emperor met disaster through poisoning, that the daughter of Lady Pan is held up to deceive the people, and an infant who cannot yet speak is set to rule the four seas.

sentences.zh: 求以徐紇、鄭儼之徒，付之司敗。

translations.literal: We request that men such as Xu Yi and Zheng Yan be handed over to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: We request that men such as Xu Yi and Zheng Yan be handed over to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 更召宗親，推其明德。

translations.literal: Let imperial kin be summoned anew and one of virtuous merit be raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Let imperial kin be summoned anew and one of virtuous merit be raised up.

sentences.zh: 」於是將赴京師。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he prepared to march on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he prepared to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈太后甚懼，詔以李神軌為大都督，將于太行杜防。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was greatly afraid; an edict appointed Li Shengui as Supreme Commander and deployed defenses at the Taihang mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was greatly afraid. An edict appointed Li Shengui as Supreme Commander and deployed defenses at the Taihang mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 榮抗表之始，遣從子天光、親信奚毅及倉頭王相入洛，與從弟世隆密議廢立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Rong's memorial campaign, he sent his nephew Tiangguang, trusted follower Xi Yi, and a household slave Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with his cousin Shilong on deposing and enthroning.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Rong's campaign, he sent his nephew Tiangguang, trusted follower Xi Yi, and a household slave Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with his cousin Shilong on deposing and enthroning.

sentences.zh: 天光乃見莊帝，具論榮心，帝許之。

translations.literal: Tiangguang then saw Emperor Zhuang, fully explained Rong's intent, and the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang then saw Emperor Zhuang, fully explained Rong's intent, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 天光等還北，榮發晉陽，猶疑所立，乃以銅鑄孝文及咸陽王禧等五王子孫像，成者當奉為主。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang and the others returned north, Rong set out from Jinyang but still doubted whom to enthrone; he had bronze cast into images of Emperor Xiaowen and the five princes' descendants of Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi, etc.—whoever's image succeeded would be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang and the others returned north, Rong set out from Jinyang but still doubted whom to enthrone. He had bronze cast into images of Emperor Xiaowen and the descendants of the five princes including Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi—whoever's image succeeded would be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 唯莊帝獨就。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Zhuang's image came out whole.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Zhuang's image came out whole.

sentences.zh: 師次河內，重遣王相密迎莊帝與帝兄彭城王邵、弟始平王子正。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to escort Emperor Zhuang, the emperor's elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Shao, and his younger brother Prince of Shiping Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to escort Emperor Zhuang, the emperor's elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Shao, and his younger brother Prince of Shiping Zizheng.

sentences.zh: 武泰元年四月，莊帝自高渚度，至榮軍，將士咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Wutai, Emperor Zhuang crossed from Gaozhu and reached Rong's army; officers and soldiers all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Wutai, Emperor Zhuang crossed from Gaozhu and reached Rong's army. Officers and soldiers all shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝即位，詔以榮為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、開府、尚書令、領軍將軍、領左右、太原王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, area commander over all military affairs within and without, Grand General, with Opening of a Government Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Palace Garrison, Commander of the Left and Right Guards, and Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, area commander over all military affairs within and without, Grand General, with Opening of a Government Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Palace Garrison, Commander of the Left and Right Guards, and Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及度河，太后乃下發入道，內外百官皆向河橋迎駕。

translations.literal: After crossing the river, the empress dowager at last renounced the world and entered religious life; within and without, the hundred officials all turned toward Heqiao Bridge to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river, the empress dowager at last renounced the world and entered religious life. Within and without, the hundred officials all turned toward Heqiao Bridge to welcome the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 榮惑武衛將軍費穆之言，謂天下乘機可取，乃譎朝士共為盟誓，將向河陰西北三里。

translations.literal: Rong, swayed by the words of General of the Martial Guard Fei Mu, believed the realm could be seized by taking advantage of the moment; he deceived the court officials into swearing a joint oath and led them three li northwest of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, swayed by the words of General of the Martial Guard Fei Mu, believed the realm could be seized by taking advantage of the moment. He deceived the court officials into swearing a joint oath and led them three li northwest of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 至南北長堤，悉命下馬西度，即遣胡騎四面圍之。

translations.literal: Reaching the north-south long embankment, he ordered all to dismount and cross westward; he then sent barbarian cavalry to surround them on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the north-south long embankment, he ordered all to dismount and cross westward, then sent barbarian cavalry to surround them on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 妄言丞相高陽王欲反，殺百官王公卿士二千餘人，皆斂手就戮。

translations.literal: Falsely claiming that Chancellor Gao Yang Wang intended rebellion, he killed more than two thousand court officials, princes, dukes, and ministers—all folded their hands and submitted to slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Falsely claiming that Chancellor Gao Yang Wang intended rebellion, he killed more than two thousand court officials, princes, dukes, and ministers—all folded their hands and submitted to slaughter.

sentences.zh: 又命二三十人拔刀走行宮。

translations.literal: He also ordered twenty or thirty men to draw blades and run toward the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered twenty or thirty men to draw blades and run toward the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 莊帝及彭城王、霸城王俱出帳。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang and the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng all came out of the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang and the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng all came out of the tent.

sentences.zh: 榮先遣并州人郭羅察共西部高車叱列殺鬼在帝左右，相與為應。

translations.literal: Rong first sent Bingzhou man Guo Luocha together with the Western Department's Gao-che warrior Chilie to kill demons at the emperor's side, acting in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Rong first sent Bingzhou man Guo Luocha together with the Western Department's Gao-che warrior Chilie to kill demons at the emperor's side, acting in concert.

sentences.zh: 及見事起，假言防衛，抱帝入帳，餘人即害彭城、霸城二王。

translations.literal: When the incident began, pretending to guard against attack, he embraced the emperor into the tent; the others at once killed the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the incident began, pretending to guard against attack, he embraced the emperor into the tent while the others at once killed the Princes of Pengcheng and Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 乃令四五十人遷帝於河橋，沉靈太后及少主於河。

translations.literal: He then had forty or fifty men move the emperor to Heqiao Bridge and drowned Empress Dowager Ling and the young ruler in the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then had forty or fifty men move the emperor to Heqiao Bridge and drowned Empress Dowager Ling and the young ruler in the river.

sentences.zh: 時又有朝士百餘人後至，仍於堤東被圍。

translations.literal: At the time another hundred-odd court officials arrived late and were again surrounded east of the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time another hundred-odd court officials arrived late and were again surrounded east of the embankment.

sentences.zh: 遂臨以白刃，唱云：「能為禪文者出，當原其命。

translations.literal: They were menaced with naked blades and told: "Whoever can draft an abdication document may come forth—his life will be spared.
translations.idiomatic: They were menaced with naked blades and told: "Whoever can draft an abdication document may come forth—his life will be spared.

sentences.zh: 」時有隴西李神俊、頓丘李諧、太原溫子升並當世辭人，皆在圍中，恥是從命，俯伏不應。

translations.literal: " At the time Longxi Li Shenjun, Dunqiu Li Xie, and Taiyuan Wen Zisheng—all leading literary men of the age—were in the encirclement; ashamed to obey, they prostrated themselves and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Longxi Li Shenjun, Dunqiu Li Xie, and Taiyuan Wen Zisheng—all leading literary men of the age—were in the encirclement. Ashamed to obey, they prostrated themselves and did not respond.

sentences.zh: 有御史趙元則者，恐不免死，出作禪文。

translations.literal: There was an imperial censor named Zhao Yuanze who, fearing he could not escape death, came forth and composed the abdication text.
translations.idiomatic: There was an imperial censor named Zhao Yuanze who, fearing he could not escape death, came forth and composed the abdication text.

sentences.zh: 榮令人誡軍士，言元氏既滅，尒硃氏興。

translations.literal: Rong had the soldiers admonished, declaring that the Yuan clan was destroyed and the Er Zhurong clan would rise.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had the soldiers admonished, declaring that the Yuan clan was destroyed and the Er Zhurong clan would rise.

sentences.zh: 其眾咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The host all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The host all shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 榮遂鑄金為己像，數四不成。

translations.literal: Rong then had a gold image of himself cast, but four attempts did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then had a gold image of himself cast, but four attempts failed.

sentences.zh: 時榮所信幽州人劉靈助善卜占，言今時人事未可。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Lingzhu of Youzhou, whom Rong trusted, was skilled in divination and said the affairs of the age were not yet suitable.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Lingzhu of Youzhou, whom Rong trusted, was skilled in divination and said the affairs of the age were not yet suitable.

sentences.zh: 榮乃曰：「若我作不吉，當迎天穆立之。

translations.literal: Rong then said: "If it is inauspicious for me to take the throne, we should welcome Tianmu and enthrone him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then said: "If it is inauspicious for me to take the throne, we should welcome Tianmu and enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 」靈助曰：「天穆亦不吉，唯長樂王有王兆耳。

translations.literal: " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu is also inauspicious—only the Prince of Changle shows the signs of kingship.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu is also inauspicious—only the Prince of Changle shows the signs of kingship.

sentences.zh: 」榮亦精神恍惚，不自支持，遂便愧悔。

translations.literal: " Rong too felt his spirit waver and could not steady himself; thereupon he was overcome with shame and remorse.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong too felt his spirit waver and could not steady himself. Thereupon he was overcome with shame and remorse.

sentences.zh: 至四更中，乃迎莊帝，望馬首叩頭請死。

translations.literal: Around the fourth watch he welcomed Emperor Zhuang back, looked toward his horse's head, and kowtowed begging for death.
translations.idiomatic: Around the fourth watch he welcomed Emperor Zhuang back, looked toward his horse's head, and kowtowed begging for death.

sentences.zh: 其士馬三千餘騎，既濫殺朝士，乃不敢入京，即欲向北為移都之計。

translations.literal: His three thousand-odd riders, having wantonly slaughtered court officials, dared not enter the capital and wished to flee north to plan moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His three thousand-odd riders, having wantonly slaughtered court officials, dared not enter the capital and wished to flee north to plan moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 持疑經日，始奉駕向洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Hesitating for days, he at last escorted the imperial carriage toward the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitating for days, he at last escorted the imperial carriage toward the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 及上北芒，視城闕，復懷畏懼，不肯更前。

translations.literal: When they ascended Beimang and looked upon the city towers, he again was filled with fear and refused to advance further.
translations.idiomatic: When they ascended Beimang and looked upon the city towers, he again was filled with fear and refused to advance further.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍汎禮苦執不聽，復前入城，不朝戍。

translations.literal: General of the Martial Guard Fan Li stubbornly held on and would not listen; he pressed forward again to enter the city and did not attend the dawn audience.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Fan Li stubbornly pressed forward to enter the city and did not attend the dawn audience.

sentences.zh: 北來之人，皆乘馬入殿。

translations.literal: Men from the north all rode horses into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Men from the north all rode horses into the hall.

sentences.zh: 諸貴死散，無復次序。

translations.literal: The grandees, dead or scattered, no longer maintained any order.
translations.idiomatic: The grandees, dead or scattered, no longer maintained any order.

sentences.zh: 莊帝左右，唯有故舊數人。

translations.literal: At Emperor Zhuang's side there remained only a few old associates.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Zhuang's side there remained only a few old associates.

sentences.zh: 榮猶執移都之議，上亦無以拒焉。

translations.literal: Rong still pressed the plan to move the capital, and the emperor could not refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong still pressed the plan to move the capital, and the emperor could not refuse him.

sentences.zh: 又在明光殿重謝河橋之事，誓言無復二心。

translations.literal: Again in the Mingguang Hall he apologized deeply for the Heyin affair and swore he would never again harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Again in the Mingguang Hall he apologized deeply for the Heyin affair and swore he would never again harbor a second heart.

sentences.zh: 莊帝自起止之，因復為榮誓，言無疑心。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang himself rose to stop him, and in turn swore to Rong that he held no doubt in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang himself rose to stop him and in turn swore to Rong that he held no doubt in his heart.

sentences.zh: 榮喜，因求酒一遍。

translations.literal: Rong was pleased and therefore asked for wine and had one full round.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was pleased and asked for wine and had one full round.

sentences.zh: 及醉熟，帝欲誅之，左右苦諫乃止。

translations.literal: When he was deeply drunk, the emperor wished to execute him but those at his side strenuously remonstrated and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When he was deeply drunk, the emperor wished to execute him, but those at his side strenuously remonstrated and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 即以床輦向中常侍省。

translations.literal: He was carried on a litter into the Directorate of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried on a litter into the Directorate of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 榮夜半方寤，遂達旦不眠。

translations.literal: Rong only awoke at midnight and did not sleep from then until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Rong only awoke at midnight and did not sleep from then until dawn.

sentences.zh: 自此不復禁中宿矣。

translations.literal: From this he no longer spent the night within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: From this he no longer spent the night within the palace.

sentences.zh: 榮女先為明帝嬪，欲上立為後，帝疑未決。

translations.literal: Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Ming; he wished the emperor to install her as empress, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Ming. He wished the emperor to install her as empress, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎祖瑩曰：「昔文公在秦，懷嬴入侍。

translations.literal: Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zu Ying said: "In former times Duke Wen of Jin while in Qin had Huai Ying enter to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zu Ying said: "In former times Duke Wen of Jin while in Qin had Huai Ying enter to serve him.

sentences.zh: 事有反經合義，陛下獨何疑焉？

translations.literal: There are matters that run counter to the norm yet accord with righteousness—why should Your Majesty alone hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: There are matters that run counter to the norm yet accord with righteousness—why should Your Majesty alone hesitate?

sentences.zh: 」上遂從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 榮意甚悅。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 于時，人間猶或云榮欲遷都晉陽，或云欲肆兵大掠，迭相驚恐，人情駭震。

translations.literal: At the time among the people some still said Rong intended to move the capital to Jinyang, or that he intended to unleash his troops in great plunder; alarm spread in waves, and popular sentiment was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: At the time among the people some still said Rong intended to move the capital to Jinyang, or that he intended to unleash his troops in great plunder. Alarm spread in waves, and popular sentiment was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 京邑士子，十不一存，率皆逃竄，無敢出者，直衛空虛，官守廢曠。

translations.literal: Of the scholars in the capital, not one in ten remained; most had fled and hidden, none dared go out. The palace guard stood empty, and official posts lay abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of the scholars in the capital, not one in ten remained. Most had fled and hidden, and none dared go out. The palace guard stood empty, and official posts lay abandoned.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，上書謝愆。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong heard of this, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault.

sentences.zh: 無上王請追尊帝號；

translations.literal: The Supreme King requested posthumous imperial honors;
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme King requested posthumous imperial honors;

sentences.zh: 諸王、刺史，乞贈三司；

translations.literal: princes and inspectors requested posthumous appointment to the Three Dukes;
translations.idiomatic: princes and inspectors requested posthumous appointment to the Three Dukes;

sentences.zh: 其位班三品，請贈令僕；

translations.literal: those of third rank requested posthumous appointment as Director or Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: those of third rank requested posthumous appointment as Director or Vice Director;

sentences.zh: 五品之官，各贈方伯；

translations.literal: fifth-rank officials each requested posthumous appointment as regional governor;
translations.idiomatic: fifth-rank officials each requested posthumous appointment as regional governor;

sentences.zh: 六品已下及白身，贈以鎮郡。

translations.literal: those of sixth rank and below, and commoners, requested posthumous enfeoffment as commandery or garrison lord.
translations.idiomatic: those of sixth rank and below, and commoners, requested posthumous enfeoffment as commandery or garrison lord.

sentences.zh: 諸死者無後，聽繼，即授封爵。

translations.literal: For the dead who had no heirs, adoption was permitted and enfeoffment was granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: For the dead who had no heirs, adoption was permitted and enfeoffment was granted at once.

sentences.zh: 均其高下，節級別科，使恩洽存亡，有慰生死。

translations.literal: Their ranks were balanced high and low, graded by degree and category, so that grace reached both the living and the dead and comfort was given to both life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Their ranks were balanced high and low, graded by degree and category, so that grace reached both the living and the dead and comfort was given to both life and death.

sentences.zh: 詔從所表。

translations.literal: An edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 又啟帝，遣使巡城勞問。

translations.literal: He also petitioned the emperor to send envoys to tour the city and offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned the emperor to send envoys to tour the city and offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 於是人情遂安，朝士逃亡者，亦稍來歸闕。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular sentiment settled, and court officials who had fled also gradually returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon popular sentiment settled, and court officials who had fled also gradually returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 榮又奏請番直，朔望之日，引見三公、令、僕、尚書、九卿及司州牧、河南尹、洛陽河陰執事之官，參論國政，以為常式。

translations.literal: Rong also memorialized requesting rotating duty: on the first and fifteenth of each month, to summon the Three Dukes, Directors, Vice Directors, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, and the officials in charge of Sizhou, Henan, Luoyang, and Heyin to discuss state affairs as a regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also memorialized requesting rotating duty: on the first and fifteenth of each month, to summon the Three Dukes, Directors, Vice Directors, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, and the officials in charge of Sizhou, Henan, Luoyang, and Heyin to discuss state affairs as a regular practice.

sentences.zh: 五月，榮還晉陽，乃令元天穆向京，為侍中、太尉公、錄尚書事、京畿大都督，兼領軍將軍，封上党王，樹置腹心在列職，舉止所為，皆由其意。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang and sent Yuan Tianmu to the capital as Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing Affairs, Supreme Commander of the Capital Region, concurrently General of the Palace Garrison, enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang. He planted trusted men in official posts; their conduct and actions all followed his will.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang and sent Yuan Tianmu to the capital as Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing Affairs, Supreme Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently General of the Palace Garrison, enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang. He planted trusted men in official posts, and their conduct followed his will.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔加榮柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict added to Rong the title of Pillar-of-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict added to Rong the title of Pillar-of-State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮向京師，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: At the time Ge Rong was marching on the capital, his host claiming a million men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ge Rong was marching on the capital, his host claiming a million men.

sentences.zh: 州刺史李神俊閉門自守。

translations.literal: Inspector Li Shenjun of the province closed the gates and held in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Li Shenjun of the province closed the gates and held in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 榮率精騎七千，馬皆有副，倍道兼行，東出滏口。

translations.literal: Rong led seven thousand elite cavalry, each horse with a spare mount, marching at double speed east out of Fuyu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Rong led seven thousand elite cavalry, each horse with a spare mount, marching at double speed east out of Fuyu Pass.

sentences.zh: 而與葛榮眾寡非敵。

translations.literal: Yet compared with Ge Rong his forces were no match in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet compared with Ge Rong his forces were no match in numbers.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，喜見於色，乃令其眾辦長繩，至便縛取。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong heard of this, joy showed on his face; he ordered his troops to prepare long ropes—to bind and capture them on arrival.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong heard of this, joy showed on his face. He ordered his troops to prepare long ropes—to bind and capture them on arrival.

sentences.zh: 自鄴以北，列陣數十里，箕張而進。

translations.literal: From Ye northward he arrayed his lines for several tens of li, advancing with wings spread like a winnowing basket.
translations.idiomatic: From Ye northward he arrayed his lines for several tens of li, advancing with wings spread like a winnowing basket.

sentences.zh: 榮潛軍山谷為奇兵，分督將已上三人為一處，處有數百騎，令所在揚塵鼓噪，使賊不測多少。

translations.literal: Rong hid troops in the valleys as a surprise force, grouping area commanders and above three to a unit, each unit with several hundred cavalry, ordering them to raise dust and clamor everywhere so the bandits could not gauge their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hid troops in the valleys as a surprise force, grouping area commanders and above three to a unit, each with several hundred cavalry, ordering them to raise dust and clamor everywhere so the bandits could not gauge their numbers.

sentences.zh: 又以人馬逼戰，刀不如棒。

translations.literal: He also held that in close combat between men and horses, blades were inferior to clubs.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that in close combat between men and horses, blades were inferior to clubs.

sentences.zh: 密勒軍士，馬上各齎袖棒一枚，至戰時，慮廢騰逐，不聽斬級，使以棒，棒之而已。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered the soldiers each to carry a sleeve club on horseback; when battle came, fearing that pursuit would be wasted on taking heads, he forbade decapitation and had them use clubs—club them and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered each soldier to carry a sleeve club on horseback. When battle came, fearing pursuit would be wasted on taking heads, he forbade decapitation and had them use clubs—club them and that was all.

sentences.zh: 乃分命壯勇，所當衝突。

translations.literal: He then assigned the strong and brave to the points of impact.
translations.idiomatic: He then assigned the strong and brave to the points of impact.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴明，將士同奮。

translations.literal: Commands were stern and clear; officers and soldiers fought as one.
translations.idiomatic: Commands were stern and clear, and officers and soldiers fought as one.

sentences.zh: 身自陷陣，出於賊後，表裏合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He personally plunged into the formation, emerging behind the bandits; inner and outer forces struck together and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He personally plunged into the formation and emerged behind the bandits. Inner and outer forces struck together and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 于陣禽葛榮，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: On the field he captured Ge Rong; the remaining host all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the field he captured Ge Rong, and the remaining host all submitted.

sentences.zh: 榮恐其疑懼，乃普令各從所樂，親屬相隨，任所居止。

translations.literal: Rong feared they would grow suspicious and afraid, and therefore broadly ordered each to follow his own wish, kin accompanying kin, free to settle where they would.
translations.idiomatic: Rong feared they would grow suspicious and afraid and therefore broadly ordered each to follow his own wish, kin accompanying kin, free to settle where they would.

sentences.zh: 於是群情喜悅，登即四散，數十萬眾，一朝散盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the mass sentiment was joyful; at once they scattered in all directions—several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the mass sentiment was joyful. At once they scattered in all directions—several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 待出百里之外，乃始分道押領，隨便安置，咸得其宜。

translations.literal: Only after they had gone beyond a hundred li did he begin to divide routes and escort them, settling each as suited—all found their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they had gone beyond a hundred li did he begin to divide routes and escort them, settling each as suited—all found their proper place.

sentences.zh: 獲其渠帥，量才授用，新附者咸安。

translations.literal: He captured their chieftains, assigned posts according to talent, and the newly attached all were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: He captured their chieftains, assigned posts according to talent, and the newly attached were all reassured.

sentences.zh: 時人服其處分機速。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his swift and decisive handling.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired his swift and decisive handling.

sentences.zh: 乃檻車送葛榮赴闕。

translations.literal: He then sent Ge Rong to the capital in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Ge Rong to the capital in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 詔加榮大丞相、都督河北畿外諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict added to Rong the titles of Grand Chancellor and area commander over all military affairs in Hebei and beyond the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added to Rong the titles of Grand Chancellor and area commander over all military affairs in Hebei and beyond the capital region.

sentences.zh: 初，榮將討葛榮，軍次襄垣，遂大獵，有雙兔起于馬前，榮彎弓誓之曰：「中則禽葛榮，不中則否。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, the army halted at Xiangyuan and held a great hunt; a pair of hares rose before his horse. Rong bent his bow and vowed: "If I hit them, I shall capture Ge Rong; if not, I shall not.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, the army halted at Xiangyuan and held a great hunt. A pair of hares rose before his horse. Rong bent his bow and vowed: "If I hit them, I shall capture Ge Rong; if not, I shall not.

sentences.zh: 」既而並應弦而殪，三軍咸悅。

translations.literal: " Both then fell to the bowstring; the whole army rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: " Both then fell to the bowstring, and the whole army rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 及後，命立碑於其所，號雙兔碑。

translations.literal: Later he ordered a stele erected at that place, called the Twin Hares Stele.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ordered a stele erected at that place, called the Twin Hares Stele.

sentences.zh: 又將戰，夜夢一人從葛榮索千牛刀，葛榮初不肯與，此人自稱己是道武皇帝，葛榮乃奉刀，此人手持授榮。

translations.literal: Again before battle he dreamed that a man demanded the imperial blade from Ge Rong; Ge Rong at first refused to give it. The man declared himself Emperor Daowu; Ge Rong then presented the blade, and the man handed it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Again before battle he dreamed that a man demanded the imperial blade from Ge Rong. Ge Rong at first refused. The man declared himself Emperor Daowu; Ge Rong then presented the blade, and the man handed it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 寤而喜。

translations.literal: Awakening, he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening, he was pleased.

sentences.zh: 自知必勝。

translations.literal: He knew he would surely win.
translations.idiomatic: He knew he would surely win.

sentences.zh: 又詔以冀州之長樂、相州之南趙、定州之博陵、滄州之浮陽、平州之遼西、燕州之上穀、幽州之漁陽七郡，各萬戶，通前滿十萬。

translations.literal: Another edict granted seven commanderies—Changle of Jizhou, Nanzhao of Xiangzhou, Boling of Dingzhou, Fuyang of Cangzhou, Liaoxi of Pingzhou, Shanggu of Yanzhou, and Yuyang of Youzhou—each ten thousand households, together with prior grants totaling one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict granted seven commanderies—Changle of Jizhou, Nanzhao of Xiangzhou, Boling of Dingzhou, Fuyang of Cangzhou, Liaoxi of Pingzhou, Shanggu of Yanzhou, and Yuyang of Youzhou—each ten thousand households, together with prior grants totaling one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 為太原國邑，又加位太師。

translations.literal: This formed the fief-state of Taiyuan, and he was further given the rank of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: This formed the fief-state of Taiyuan, and he was further given the rank of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 建義初，北海王元顥南奔梁，梁立為魏主，資以兵將。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyi era, Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao fled south to Liang; Liang enthroned him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era, Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao fled south to Liang. Liang enthroned him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals.

sentences.zh: 時邢杲以三齊應顥。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Gao raised the Three Qis in response to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xing Gao raised the Three Qis in response to Hao.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以顥孤弱，永安二年春，詔元天穆先平齊地，然後征顥。

translations.literal: The court judged Hao isolated and weak; in the spring of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered Yuan Tianmu first to pacify Qi territory, then campaign against Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Hao isolated and weak. In the spring of the second year of Yong'an an edict ordered Yuan Tianmu first to pacify Qi territory, then campaign against Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥乘虛徑進，榮陽、武牢並不守，車駕出居河北。

translations.literal: Hao seized the opening and pressed straight forward; Rongyang and Wulao both went undefended, and the imperial carriage withdrew to dwell north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized the opening and pressed straight forward. Rongyang and Wulao both went undefended, and the imperial carriage withdrew north of the river.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，馳傳朝行宮於上党之長子，輿駕於是南趣。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this, he raced by post to attend the traveling palace at Changzi in Shangdang; the imperial carriage thereupon turned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong heard of this, he raced by post to attend the traveling palace at Changzi in Shangdang. The imperial carriage thereupon turned south.

sentences.zh: 榮為前驅，旬日之間，兵馬大集。

translations.literal: Rong served as vanguard; within ten days troops and horses massed in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong served as vanguard. Within ten days troops and horses massed in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 天穆克平邢杲，亦度河以會。

translations.literal: Tianmu conquered and pacified Xing Gao and also crossed the river to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu conquered and pacified Xing Gao and also crossed the river to join him.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸河內。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage visited Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮與顥相持於河上，無船不得即度。

translations.literal: Rong and Hao faced each other across the river; without boats they could not cross at once.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Hao faced each other across the river. Without boats they could not cross at once.

sentences.zh: 議欲還北，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Some deliberated on returning north to plan a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Some deliberated on returning north to plan a later effort.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎楊侃、高道穆等並固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all stubbornly held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all stubbornly held that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 屬馬渚諸楊雲有小船數艘，求為鄉導。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Yun of Mazhu had several small boats and offered to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Yang Yun of Mazhu had several small boats and offered to serve as guide.

sentences.zh: 榮乃令都督尒硃兆等率精騎夜濟。

translations.literal: Rong then ordered area commander Er Zhurong Zhao and others to lead elite cavalry across by night.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then ordered area commander Er Zhurong Zhao and others to lead elite cavalry across by night.

sentences.zh: 顥奔。

translations.literal: Hao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hao fled.

sentences.zh: 車駕度河，入居華林園。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river and entered to dwell in Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage crossed the river and entered to dwell in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 詔加榮天柱大將軍，增封通前二十萬戶，加前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: An edict added to Rong the title of Pillar-of-Heaven Grand General, increased his fief by two hundred thousand households including prior grants, and added front and rear feathered banners and drum-and-flute escort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added to Rong the title of Pillar-of-Heaven Grand General, increased his fief by two hundred thousand households including prior grants, and added front and rear feathered banners and drum-and-flute escort.

sentences.zh: 榮尋還晉陽，遙制朝廷，親戚腹心，皆補要職，百僚朝廷動靜，莫不以申。

translations.literal: Rong soon returned to Jinyang and controlled the court from afar; kin and trusted men all filled key posts, and the movements of the hundred officials and the court were all reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong soon returned to Jinyang and controlled the court from afar. Kin and trusted men filled key posts, and the movements of the hundred officials and the court were all reported to him.

sentences.zh: 至於除授，皆須榮許，然後得用。

translations.literal: As for appointments and dismissals, all required Rong's approval before they could take effect.
translations.idiomatic: As for appointments and dismissals, all required Rong's approval before they could take effect.

sentences.zh: 莊帝雖受制權臣，而勤政事，朝夕省納，孜孜不已。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Zhuang was constrained by the powerful minister, he diligently attended to affairs of state, reviewing and accepting matters morning and evening without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Zhuang was constrained by the powerful minister, he diligently attended to affairs of state, reviewing and accepting matters morning and evening without cease.

sentences.zh: 數自理冤獄，親覽辭訟。

translations.literal: He repeatedly personally cleared wrongful cases and personally reviewed petitions and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly personally cleared wrongful cases and reviewed petitions and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 又選司多濫，與吏部尚書李神俊議正綱紀。

translations.literal: Also the selection offices were much abused; he discussed with Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenjun correcting discipline and order.
translations.idiomatic: The selection offices were much abused, and he discussed with Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenjun correcting discipline and order.

sentences.zh: 而榮乃大相嫌責。

translations.literal: But Rong greatly resented and rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: But Rong greatly resented and rebuked this.

sentences.zh: 曾關補定州曲陽縣令，神俊以階縣不奏，別更擬人。

translations.literal: Once he intervened to appoint the magistrate of Quyang County in Dingzhou; Shenjun, because it was a county of lower grade, did not memorialize it and proposed someone else instead.
translations.idiomatic: Once he intervened to appoint the magistrate of Quyang County in Dingzhou. Shenjun, because it was a county of lower grade, did not memorialize it and proposed someone else instead.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，即遣其所補者往奪其任。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly enraged and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was greatly enraged and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post.

sentences.zh: 榮使入京，雖復微蔑，朝貴見之，莫不傾靡。

translations.literal: When Rong's envoys entered the capital, though they were again somewhat contemptuous, the court grandees who saw them all bowed and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong's envoys entered the capital, though they were again somewhat contemptuous, the court grandees who saw them all bowed and yielded.

sentences.zh: 及至闕下，未得通奏，恃榮威勢，至乃忿怒。

translations.literal: When they reached the palace gates and could not get their memorials through, relying on Rong's prestige and power they even grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the palace gates and could not get their memorials through, relying on Rong's prestige and power they even grew angry.

sentences.zh: 神俊遂上表遜位。

translations.literal: Shenjun thereupon submitted a memorial yielding his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun thereupon submitted a memorial yielding his post.

sentences.zh: 榮欲用世隆攝選，上亦不違。

translations.literal: Rong wished to have Shilong act as interim selection officer; the emperor did not oppose this.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to have Shilong act as interim selection officer, and the emperor did not oppose this.

sentences.zh: 榮曾啟北人為河內諸州，欲為掎角勢，上不即從。

translations.literal: Rong once petitioned to appoint northerners to the various provinces of Henei, seeking a pincer formation; the emperor did not immediately comply.
translations.idiomatic: Rong once petitioned to appoint northerners to the various provinces of Henei, seeking a pincer formation, but the emperor did not immediately comply.

sentences.zh: 天穆入見論事，上猶未許。

translations.literal: Tianmu entered audience to discuss the matter; the emperor still did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu entered audience to discuss the matter, but the emperor still did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 天穆曰：「天柱既有大功，為國宰相，若請普代天下官屬，恐陛下亦不得違。

translations.literal: Tianmu said: "The Pillar of Heaven has already achieved great merit and serves as the state's chancellor—if he requested to replace all officials under heaven, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu said: "The Pillar of Heaven has already achieved great merit and serves as the state's chancellor—if he requested to replace all officials under heaven, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either.

sentences.zh: 如何啟數人為州，便停不用？

translations.literal: How then, when he petitions for a few men as provincial governors, can you halt and not use them?
translations.idiomatic: How then, when he petitions for a few men as provincial governors, can you halt and not use them?

sentences.zh: 」帝正色曰：「天柱若不為人臣，朕亦須代；

translations.literal: The emperor said sternly: "If the Pillar of Heaven is no longer a subject, I too must be replaced;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said sternly: "If the Pillar of Heaven is no longer a subject, I too must be replaced;

sentences.zh: 如其猶存臣節，無代天下百官理。

translations.literal: if he still preserves the integrity of a subject, there is no reason to replace all officials under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: if he still preserves the integrity of a subject, there is no reason to replace all officials under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」榮聞，大怒曰：「天子由誰得立？

translations.literal: " When Rong heard this, he raged: "By whose agency did the Son of Heaven gain the throne?
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong heard this, he raged: "By whose agency did the Son of Heaven gain the throne?

sentences.zh: 今乃不用我！

translations.literal: And now he will not use me!
translations.idiomatic: And now he will not use me!

sentences.zh: 」語皇后復嫌內妃嬪甚有妒恨之事。

translations.literal: " He spoke to the empress, who again resented the inner consorts and had much jealousy and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke to the empress, who again resented the inner consorts and harbored much jealousy and hatred.

sentences.zh: 帝遣世隆語以大理，後曰：「天子由我家置立，今便如此。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shilong to explain the larger principle; the empress said: "The Son of Heaven was installed by our house—now it comes to this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shilong to explain the larger principle. The empress said: "The Son of Heaven was installed by our house—now it comes to this.

sentences.zh: 我父本日即自作，今亦復決？

translations.literal: My father could have made himself ruler that very day—is the matter still undecided?
translations.idiomatic: My father could have made himself ruler that very day—is the matter still undecided?

sentences.zh: 」世隆曰：「兄止自不為，若本自作，臣今亦得封王。

translations.literal: Shilong said: "My elder brother simply chose not to do so—if he had made himself ruler from the start, I too would now be enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said: "My elder brother simply chose not to do so—if he had made himself ruler from the start, I too would now be enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 」帝既外迫強臣，內逼皇后，恆怏怏不以萬乘為貴。

translations.literal: " The emperor, pressed without by the powerful minister and within by the empress, was constantly discontent and did not regard the imperial throne as precious.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, pressed without by the powerful minister and within by the empress, was constantly discontent and did not regard the imperial throne as precious.

sentences.zh: 先是，葛榮枝党韓婁仍據幽、平二州，榮遣都督侯深討斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's faction, still held the two provinces of You and Ping; Rong sent area commander Hou Shen to campaign against and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's faction, still held the two provinces of You and Ping. Rong sent area commander Hou Shen to campaign against and behead him.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤擁眾豳、涇，榮遣其從子天光為雍州刺史，令率都督賀拔岳、侯莫陳悅等入關討之。

translations.literal: At the time Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held masses in Bin and Jing; Rong sent his nephew Tiangguang as Inspector of Yongzhou, ordering him to lead area commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others to enter the passes and campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held masses in Bin and Jing. Rong sent his nephew Tiangguang as Inspector of Yongzhou, ordering him to lead area commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others to enter the passes and campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 天光至雍州，以眾少未進。

translations.literal: Tiangguang reached Yongzhou but did not advance because his forces were too few.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang reached Yongzhou but did not advance because his forces were too few.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，遣其騎兵參軍劉貴馳驛詣軍，加天光杖罰。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly enraged and sent his Cavalry Adjutant Liu Gui by post to the army to add corporal punishment to Tiangguang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was greatly enraged and sent his Cavalry Adjutant Liu Gui by post to the army to have Tiangguang beaten.

sentences.zh: 天光等大懼，乃進討，連破之，禽醜奴、寶夤，並檻車送闕。

translations.literal: Tiangguang and the others were greatly afraid and therefore advanced to campaign, defeating them in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending both to the capital in caged carts.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang and the others were greatly afraid and advanced to campaign, defeating them in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending both to the capital in caged carts.

sentences.zh: 天光又禽王慶雲、万俟道樂，關中悉平。

translations.literal: Tiangguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo; all of Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daoluo, and all of Guanzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是天下大難便盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great calamities of the realm were at an end.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the great calamities of the realm were at an end.

sentences.zh: 莊帝恆不慮外寇，唯恐榮為逆。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang constantly gave no thought to foreign invaders and feared only that Rong would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang constantly gave no thought to foreign invaders and feared only that Rong would rebel.

sentences.zh: 常時諸方未定，欲使與之相持。

translations.literal: While the various regions were still unsettled, he wished to keep them in mutual stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: While the various regions were still unsettled, he wished to keep them in mutual stalemate.

sentences.zh: 及告捷之日，乃不甚喜，謂尚書令、臨淮王彧曰：「即今天下，便是無賊？

translations.literal: On the day victory was reported, he was not greatly pleased and said to Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Linhuai Yu: "So the realm is now entirely free of bandits?
translations.idiomatic: On the day victory was reported, he was not greatly pleased and said to Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Linhuai Yu: "So the realm is now entirely free of bandits?

sentences.zh: 」臨淮見帝色不悅，曰：「臣恐賊平以後，方勞聖慮。

translations.literal: " Prince of Linhuai, seeing the emperor's displeased expression, said: "Your servant fears that after the bandits are pacified, Your Majesty's concerns will only begin.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince of Linhuai, seeing the emperor's displeased expression, said: "Your servant fears that after the bandits are pacified, Your Majesty's concerns will only begin.

sentences.zh: 」帝畏餘人怪，還以他語解之，曰：「其實撫甯荒余，彌成不易。」

translations.literal: " The emperor, fearing others would find it strange, explained with other words: "In truth, pacifying and settling the devastated remnants is all the more difficult."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, fearing others would find it strange, explained with other words: "In truth, pacifying and settling the devastated remnants is all the more difficult."

sentences.zh: 榮好射獵，不舍寒暑，法禁嚴重。

translations.literal: Rong loved hunting and shooting, never ceasing winter or summer; regulations and prohibitions were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Rong loved hunting and shooting, never ceasing winter or summer. Regulations and prohibitions were severe.

sentences.zh: 若一鹿出，乃有數人殞命。

translations.literal: If a single deer appeared, several men might lose their lives.
translations.idiomatic: If a single deer appeared, several men might lose their lives.

sentences.zh: 曾有一人，見猛獸便走，謂曰：「欲求活邪！

translations.literal: Once a man, seeing a fierce beast, fled; Rong said to him: "Do you wish to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Once a man, seeing a fierce beast, fled. Rong said to him: "Do you wish to live!"

sentences.zh: 」遂即斬之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 自此獵如登戰場。

translations.literal: From this hunting was like entering a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, hunting was like entering a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 曾見一猛獸在窮穀中，乃令餘人重衣空手搏之，不令復損。

translations.literal: Once he saw a fierce beast in a remote ravine and ordered the others, in heavy clothing and empty-handed, to wrestle it, forbidding further harm to it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw a fierce beast in a remote ravine and ordered the others, in heavy clothing and empty-handed, to wrestle it, forbidding them to harm it further.

sentences.zh: 於是數人被殺，遂禽得之。

translations.literal: Thereupon several men were killed, and at last it was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Several men were killed in the attempt, but at last the beast was captured.

sentences.zh: 持此而樂焉。

translations.literal: He took pleasure in such things.
translations.idiomatic: He took pleasure in such things.

sentences.zh: 列圍而進，雖阻險不得回避，其下甚苦之。

translations.literal: He arrayed the encirclement and advanced; though the terrain was obstructive they could not avoid it, and those below suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He arrayed the encirclement and advanced. Though the terrain was obstructive, his men could not avoid it, and those below suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 太宰元天穆從容言榮勳業，宜調政養人。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu calmly spoke of Rong's achievements and said he ought to adjust governance and nurture the people.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu calmly spoke of Rong's achievements and said he ought to adjust governance and nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 榮便攘肘謂天穆曰：「太后女主，不能自正，推奉天子者，此是人臣常節。

translations.literal: Rong then dug his elbow into Tianmu and said: "The empress dowager, a woman ruler, could not set herself right; to raise up and support the Son of Heaven—this is the constant duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then dug his elbow into Tianmu and said: "The empress dowager, a woman ruler, could not set herself right. To raise up and support the Son of Heaven—this is the constant duty of a subject.

sentences.zh: 葛容之徒，本是奴才，乘時作亂，譬如奴走，禽獲便休。

translations.literal: Men such as Ge Rong were originally slaves who seized the moment to rebel—like a runaway slave, once captured the matter ends.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Ge Rong were originally slaves who seized the moment to rebel—like a runaway slave, once captured the matter ends.

sentences.zh: 頃來受國大寵，未能混一海內，何宜今日便言勳也？

translations.literal: Recently I have received the state's great favor yet have not unified the realm within the four seas—how is it fitting to speak of merit today?
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have received the state's great favor yet have not unified the realm within the four seas—how is it fitting to speak of merit today?

sentences.zh: 如聞朝士猶自寬縱，今秋欲共兄戒勒士馬，校獵嵩原，令貪汙朝貴，入圍搏虎。

translations.literal: I hear the court officials are still indulgent and lax; this autumn I wish to join you, elder brother, in drilling troops and horses, holding a hunt on Songyuan, and making the corrupt court grandees enter the ring to wrestle tigers.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the court officials are still indulgent and lax. This autumn I wish to join you, elder brother, in drilling troops and horses, holding a hunt on Songyuan, and making the corrupt court grandees enter the ring to wrestle tigers.

sentences.zh: 仍出魯陽，曆三荊，悉擁生蠻，北填六鎮。

translations.literal: Then march out from Luyang, pass through the Three Jings, gather all the raw barbarians, and fill the Six Garrisons in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Then march out from Luyang, pass through the Three Jings, gather all the raw barbarians, and fill the Six Garrisons in the north.

sentences.zh: 回軍之際，因平汾胡。

translations.literal: On the return march, pacify the Fen Hu along the way.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, pacify the Fen Hu along the way.

sentences.zh: 明年簡練精騎，分出江、淮，蕭衍若降，乞萬戶侯；

translations.literal: Next year select and drill elite cavalry, dispatch them south of the Yangtze and Huai; if Xiao Yan submits, I request a marquisate of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Next year select and drill elite cavalry and dispatch them south of the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan submits, I request a marquisate of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 如其不降，徑度數千騎，便往縛取。

translations.literal: if he does not submit, cross directly with several thousand cavalry and go bind and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: if he does not submit, cross directly with several thousand cavalry and go bind and capture him.

sentences.zh: 待六合寧一，八表無塵，然後共兄奉天子巡四方，觀風俗，布政教，如此乃可稱勳耳。

translations.literal: Wait until the six directions are at peace and the eight regions are without dust; then together with you, elder brother, escort the Son of Heaven on a tour of the four quarters, observe customs, and spread governance and teaching—only then may one speak of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the six directions are at peace and the eight regions are without dust. Then together with you, elder brother, escort the Son of Heaven on a tour of the four quarters, observe customs, and spread governance and teaching—only then may one speak of merit.

sentences.zh: 今若止獵，兵士懈怠，安可復用也？」

translations.literal: If we now stop hunting, the soldiers will grow slack—how can they be used again?"
translations.idiomatic: If we now stop hunting, the soldiers will grow slack—how can they be used again?"

sentences.zh: 及見四方無事，乃遣人奏曰：「參軍許周勸臣取九錫，臣惡其此言，已發遣令去。

translations.literal: When he saw the four quarters were without trouble, he sent a man to memorialize: "Adjutant Xu Zhou urged me to accept the Nine Bestowals; I detested these words and have already sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the four quarters were at peace, he sent a man to memorialize: "Adjutant Xu Zhou urged me to accept the Nine Bestowals. I detested these words and have already sent him away.

sentences.zh: 」榮時望得殊禮，故以意諷朝廷。

translations.literal: " Rong at the time hoped for extraordinary honors and therefore hinted at this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong at the time hoped for extraordinary honors and therefore hinted at this to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝實不欲與之，因稱其忠。

translations.literal: The emperor in truth did not wish to grant them and therefore praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in truth did not wish to grant them and therefore praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 榮見帝年長明悟，為眾所歸，欲移自近，皆使由己。

translations.literal: Rong saw that the emperor was grown, perceptive, and the object of popular allegiance; he wished to keep him close and have all matters pass through himself.
translations.idiomatic: Rong saw that the emperor was grown, perceptive, and the object of popular allegiance. He wished to keep him close and have all matters pass through himself.

sentences.zh: 每因醉雲，入將天子，拜謁金陵後，還復恆朔。

translations.literal: Whenever he was drunk as a cloud, he would enter and take the Son of Heaven to pay homage at Jinling, then return for the regular dawn audience.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was drunk as a cloud, he would enter and take the emperor to pay homage at Jinling, then return for the regular dawn audience.

sentences.zh: 而侍中硃元龍輒從尚書索太和中遷京故事，於是復有移都消息。

translations.literal: But Palace Attendant Zhu Yuanlong repeatedly requested from the Masters of Writing the precedents for moving the capital in the Taihe era, and thereupon rumors of moving the capital arose again.
translations.idiomatic: But Palace Attendant Zhu Yuanlong repeatedly requested from the Masters of Writing the precedents for moving the capital in the Taihe era, and rumors of moving the capital arose again.

sentences.zh: 榮乃暫來向京，言看皇后娩難。

translations.literal: Rong then came temporarily toward the capital, saying he wished to attend the empress's childbirth.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then came temporarily toward the capital, saying he wished to attend the empress's childbirth.

sentences.zh: 帝懲河陰之事，終恐難保，乃與城陽王徽、侍中楊侃、李彧、尚書右僕射元羅謀，皆勸帝刺殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor, chastened by the Heyin affair, ultimately feared he could not preserve himself and therefore plotted with Prince of Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Li Yu, and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo—all urged the emperor to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, chastened by the Heyin affair, ultimately feared he could not preserve himself and plotted with Prince of Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Li Yu, and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo—all urged the emperor to assassinate Rong.

sentences.zh: 唯膠東侯李侃晞、濟陰王暉業言榮若來，必有備，恐不可圖。

translations.literal: Only Marquis of Jiaodong Li Kanxi and Prince of Jiyin Huiye said that if Rong came he would surely be prepared and the plot might not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Marquis of Jiaodong Li Kanxi and Prince of Jiyin Huiye said that if Rong came he would surely be prepared and the plot might not succeed.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺其黨與，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: They also wished to kill his faction and raise troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: They also wished to kill his faction and raise troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 帝疑未定，而京師人懷憂懼，中書侍郎邢子才之徒，已避之東出。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and had not decided, while people in the capital were filled with worry and fear; Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Xing Zicai and others had already fled eastward to avoid trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and had not decided, while people in the capital were filled with worry and fear. Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Xing Zicai and others had already fled eastward.

sentences.zh: 榮乃遍與朝士書，相任留。

translations.literal: Rong then wrote letters to all court officials, mutually urging them to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then wrote letters to all court officials, mutually urging them to remain.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人溫子升以書呈帝，帝恆望其不來，及見書，以榮必來，色甚不悅。

translations.literal: Secretary of the Masters of Writing Wen Zisheng presented the letter to the emperor; the emperor had constantly hoped Rong would not come, but upon seeing the letter judged that Rong would surely come, and his expression was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary of the Masters of Writing Wen Zisheng presented the letter to the emperor. The emperor had constantly hoped Rong would not come, but upon seeing the letter judged that Rong would surely come, and his expression darkened.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍奚毅，建義初往來通命，帝每期之甚重，然以為榮通親，不敢與之言情。

translations.literal: General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, who in the early Jianyi era had gone back and forth conveying orders, the emperor always valued him highly, yet because he was Rong's close kin dared not confide his feelings to him.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi had gone back and forth conveying orders in the early Jianyi era, and the emperor always valued him highly, yet because he was Rong's close kin dared not confide his feelings to him.

sentences.zh: 毅曰：「若必有變，臣甯死陛下難，不能事契胡。

translations.literal: Yi said: "If disaster must come, your servant would rather die in Your Majesty's peril than serve the Qi-hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "If disaster must come, your servant would rather die in Your Majesty's peril than serve the Qi-hu.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕保天柱無異心，亦不忘卿忠款。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I guarantee the Pillar of Heaven harbors no second heart, and I shall not forget your loyal devotion."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "I guarantee the Pillar of Heaven harbors no second heart, and I shall not forget your loyal devotion."

sentences.zh: 三年八月，榮將四五千騎，發并州向京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Rong led four or five thousand cavalry, setting out from Bingzhou toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, Rong led four or five thousand cavalry from Bingzhou toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言其反，復道天子必應圖之。

translations.literal: People of the time all said he was rebelling, and again said the Son of Heaven must surely be plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all said he was rebelling, and again said the emperor must surely be plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 九月初，榮至京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the ninth month Rong reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the ninth month Rong reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 有人告雲，帝欲圖之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that the emperor intended to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that the emperor intended to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 榮即具奏。

translations.literal: Rong immediately submitted a full memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Rong immediately submitted a full memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「外人亦言王欲害我，豈可信之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Outsiders also say Your Highness wishes to harm me—how can such things be believed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Outsiders also say Your Highness wishes to harm me—how can such things be believed?

sentences.zh: 」於是榮不自疑，每入謁帝，從人不過數十，皆不持兵仗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Rong did not suspect himself; whenever he entered audience with the emperor, his followers numbered no more than several tens and none carried weapons.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Rong did not suspect himself. Whenever he entered audience with the emperor, his followers numbered no more than several tens and none carried weapons.

sentences.zh: 帝欲止，城陽王曰：「縱不反，亦何可耐？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to stop, but Prince of Chengyang said: "Even if he does not rebel, how can he be endured?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to stop, but Prince of Chengyang said: "Even if he does not rebel, how can he be endured?

sentences.zh: 況何可保耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, how can he be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, how can he be trusted?

sentences.zh: 」又北人語訛，語「尒硃」為「人主」。

translations.literal: " Also among northerners speech was corrupted—they pronounced "Erzhu" as "ruler."
translations.idiomatic: " Also among northerners speech was corrupted—they pronounced "Erzhu" as "ruler."

sentences.zh: 上又聞其在北言，我姓人主。

translations.literal: The emperor also heard that in the north he said, "My surname is Ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also heard that in the north Rong said, "My surname is Ruler."

sentences.zh: 先是，長星出中台，掃大角，恆州人高榮祖頗明天文，榮問之曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: Earlier, a comet appeared from the Central Terrace and swept the Great Horn; Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou was well versed in astronomy, and Rong asked him: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a comet appeared from the Central Terrace and swept the Great Horn. Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou was well versed in astronomy, and Rong asked him: "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「除舊佈新象也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "It is the sign of removing the old and spreading the new.
