translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "It is the sign of removing the old and spreading the new.

sentences.zh: 昔長星掃大角，秦以之亡。

translations.literal: In former times when a comet swept the Great Horn, Qin perished because of it.
translations.idiomatic: In former times when a comet swept the Great Horn, Qin perished because of it.

sentences.zh: 」榮聞之悅。

translations.literal: " When Rong heard this he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong heard this he was pleased.

sentences.zh: 又榮下行台郎中李顯和曾曰：「天柱至，那無九錫，安須王自索也？

translations.literal: Also Li Xianhe, a gentleman of Rong's mobile headquarters, once said: "When the Pillar of Heaven arrives, how could there be no Nine Bestowals—why must Your Highness ask for them himself?
translations.idiomatic: Also Li Xianhe, a gentleman of Rong's mobile headquarters, once said: "When the Pillar of Heaven arrives, how could there be no Nine Bestowals—why must Your Highness ask for them himself?

sentences.zh: 亦是天子不見機！

translations.literal: It is also that the Son of Heaven does not see the moment!
translations.idiomatic: It is also that the emperor does not see the moment!

sentences.zh: 」都督郭羅察曰：「今年真可作禪文，何但九錫。

translations.literal: " Area commander Guo Luocha said: "This year one could truly compose an abdication document—why stop at the Nine Bestowals?
translations.idiomatic: " Area commander Guo Luocha said: "This year one could truly compose an abdication document—why stop at the Nine Bestowals?

sentences.zh: 」參軍褚光曰：「人言并州城上有紫氣，何慮天柱不應。

translations.literal: " Adjutant Chu Guang said: "People say purple vapor rises above Bingzhou city—why worry that the Pillar of Heaven will not respond?
translations.idiomatic: " Adjutant Chu Guang said: "People say purple vapor rises above Bingzhou city—why worry that the Pillar of Heaven will not respond?

sentences.zh: 」榮下人皆陵侮帝左右，無所忌憚，其事皆上聞。

translations.literal: " All of Rong's subordinates insulted and humiliated those at the emperor's side without any restraint; all these matters reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: " All of Rong's subordinates insulted and humiliated those at the emperor's side without restraint, and all these matters reached the emperor's ears.

sentences.zh: 奚毅又見，求聞。

translations.literal: Xi Yi again had audience and requested a private hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yi again had audience and requested a private hearing.

sentences.zh: 帝即下明光殿與語。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately descended to the Mingguang Hall to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately descended to the Mingguang Hall to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 帝又疑其為榮，不告以情。

translations.literal: The emperor again suspected he was acting for Rong and did not confide the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again suspected he was acting for Rong and did not confide the truth.

sentences.zh: 及知毅赤誠，乃召城陽王徽及楊侃、李彧，告以毅語。

translations.literal: When he learned of Yi's sincere loyalty, he summoned Prince of Chengyang Hui and Yang Kan and Li Yu and told them Yi's words.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of Yi's sincere loyalty, he summoned Prince of Chengyang Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu and told them what Yi had said.

sentences.zh: 榮小女嫁與帝兄子陳留王，小字伽邪。

translations.literal: Rong's younger daughter was married to the emperor's elder brother's son, Prince of Chenliu, styled Jiaye.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger daughter was married to the emperor's elder brother's son, Prince of Chenliu, styled Jiaye.

sentences.zh: 榮嘗指之曰：「我終當得此女婿力。

translations.literal: Rong once pointed to him and said: "I shall ultimately gain this son-in-law's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Rong once pointed to him and said: "I shall ultimately gain this son-in-law's strength.

sentences.zh: 」徽又云：「榮慮陛下終為此患，脫有東宮，必貪立孩幼。

translations.literal: " Hui also said: "Rong fears Your Majesty will ultimately become this trouble; if there is an Eastern Palace heir, he will surely be eager to enthrone a child.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui also said: "Rong fears Your Majesty will ultimately become this trouble. If there is an Eastern Palace heir, he will surely be eager to enthrone a child.

sentences.zh: 若皇后不生太子，則立陳留以安天下。

translations.literal: If the empress does not bear a crown prince, then he will enthrone Chenliu to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If the empress does not bear a crown prince, then he will enthrone Chenliu to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 」並言榮指陳留語狀。

translations.literal: " He also reported Rong's words and gestures regarding Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: " He also reported Rong's words and gestures regarding Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 帝既有圖榮意，夜夢手持一刀自害，落十指節，都不覺痛。

translations.literal: The emperor, already intending to plot against Rong, dreamed at night that he held a blade and cut himself, severing the joints of ten fingers yet feeling no pain at all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already intending to plot against Rong, dreamed that he held a blade and cut himself, severing the joints of ten fingers yet feeling no pain at all.

sentences.zh: 惡之，以告城陽王徽及楊侃。

translations.literal: He found it ominous and told Prince of Chengyang Hui and Yang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He found it ominous and told Prince of Chengyang Hui and Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 徽解夢曰：「蝮蛇螫手，壯士解腕。

translations.literal: Hui interpreted the dream: "When a viper stings the hand, the stalwart cuts off his wrist.
translations.idiomatic: Hui interpreted the dream: "When a viper stings the hand, the stalwart cuts off his wrist.

sentences.zh: 割指節與解腕何異？

translations.literal: Severing finger joints—how is it different from cutting the wrist?
translations.idiomatic: Severing finger joints—how is it different from cutting the wrist?

sentences.zh: 去患乃是吉祥。

translations.literal: Removing the affliction is in fact auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the affliction is in fact auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆言善。

translations.literal: " All who heard said it was well said.
translations.idiomatic: " All who heard said it was well said.

sentences.zh: 九月十五日，天穆到京，駕迎之。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month Tianmu reached the capital; the imperial carriage went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month Tianmu reached the capital, and the imperial carriage went to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 榮與天穆並從入西林園燕射。

translations.literal: Rong and Tianmu together followed into Xilin Garden for banquet and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Tianmu together followed into Xilin Garden for banquet and archery.

sentences.zh: 榮乃奏曰：「近來侍官皆不習武，陛下宜將五百騎出獵，因省辭訟。

translations.literal: Rong then memorialized: "Recently the palace attendants are all unskilled in martial arts; Your Majesty ought to take five hundred cavalry out hunting and thereby review petitions and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then memorialized: "Recently the palace attendants are all unskilled in martial arts. Your Majesty ought to take five hundred cavalry out hunting and thereby review petitions and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 」先是奚毅言榮因獵挾天子移都，至是，其言相符。

translations.literal: " Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong would use the hunt to seize the Son of Heaven and move the capital; at this, his words matched.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong would use the hunt to seize the emperor and move the capital. At this, his words matched.

sentences.zh: 至十八日，召中書舍人溫子升告以殺榮狀，並問以殺董卓事。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth he summoned Secretary of the Masters of Writing Wen Zisheng and told him the plan to kill Rong, also asking about the killing of Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth he summoned Secretary of the Masters of Writing Wen Zisheng and told him the plan to kill Rong, also asking about the killing of Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 子升具通本，上曰：「王允若即赦涼州人，必不應至此。

translations.literal: Zisheng fully explained the original account; the emperor said: "If Wang Yun had at once pardoned the men of Liangzhou, things would surely not have reached this pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng fully explained the original account. The emperor said: "If Wang Yun had at once pardoned the men of Liangzhou, things would surely not have reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 」良久，語子升曰：「朕之情理，卿所具知，死猶須為，況必不死！

translations.literal: " After a long while he said to Zisheng: "My feelings and reasoning you fully know—even if death were certain I must act, how much more when death is not certain!
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while he said to Zisheng: "My feelings and reasoning you fully know—even if death were certain I must act, how much more when death is not certain!

sentences.zh: 甯與高貴鄉公同日死，不與常道鄉公同日生。

translations.literal: Better to die on the same day as Duke of Gaoguixiang than to live on the same day as Duke of Changdaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Better to die on the same day as Duke of Gaoguixiang than to live on the same day as Duke of Changdaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 」上謂殺榮、天穆，即赦其党，便應不動。

translations.literal: " The emperor held that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their faction pardoned at once, they would surely not stir.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor held that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their faction pardoned at once, they would surely not stir.

sentences.zh: 應詔王道習曰：「尒硃世隆、司馬子如、硃元龍比來偏被委付，具知天下虛實，謂不宜留。

translations.literal: In response to an edict Wang Daoxi said: "Er Zhurong Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong have recently been especially entrusted and fully know the realm's strengths and weaknesses—I hold they should not be kept.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an edict Wang Daoxi said: "Er Zhurong Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong have recently been especially entrusted and fully know the realm's strengths and weaknesses—I hold they should not be kept.

sentences.zh: 」城陽王及楊侃曰：「若世隆不全，仲遠、天光豈有來理？

translations.literal: " Prince of Chengyang and Yang Kan said: "If Shilong is not spared whole, how could Zhongyuan and Tiangguang have reason to come?
translations.idiomatic: " Prince of Chengyang and Yang Kan said: "If Shilong is not spared whole, how could Zhongyuan and Tiangguang have reason to come?

sentences.zh: 」帝亦謂然，無復殺意。

translations.literal: " The emperor also judged this correct and no longer harbored intent to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also judged this correct and no longer harbored intent to kill them.

sentences.zh: 城陽曰：「榮數征伐，腰間有刀，或能狠戾傷人。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang said: "Rong has campaigned many times and wears a blade at his waist—he may violently harm someone.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang said: "Rong has campaigned many times and wears a blade at his waist—he may violently harm someone.

sentences.zh: 臨事，願陛下出。

translations.literal: When the moment comes, I wish Your Majesty to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment comes, I wish Your Majesty to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」乃伏侃等十餘人於明光殿東。

translations.literal: " He then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Mingguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Mingguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 其日，榮與天穆併入，坐食未訖，起出。

translations.literal: That day Rong and Tianmu entered together; before they had finished eating they rose and went out.
translations.idiomatic: That day Rong and Tianmu entered together. Before they had finished eating they rose and went out.

sentences.zh: 侃等從東階上殿，見榮、天穆出至中庭，事不果。

translations.literal: Kan and the others ascended the hall by the eastern steps; seeing Rong and Tianmu go out to the central courtyard, the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Kan and the others ascended the hall by the eastern steps. Seeing Rong and Tianmu go out to the central courtyard, the affair did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 十九日是帝忌日。

translations.literal: The nineteenth was the emperor's death anniversary.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteenth was the emperor's death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 二十日榮忌日。

translations.literal: The twentieth was Rong's death anniversary.
translations.idiomatic: The twentieth was Rong's death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，暫入，即向陳留王家，飲酒極醉。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first he entered briefly, then went straight to Prince of Chenliu's house and drank until utterly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first he entered briefly, then went straight to Prince of Chenliu's house and drank until utterly drunk.

sentences.zh: 遂言病動，頻日不入。

translations.literal: He then claimed his illness was acting up and for several days did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed his illness was acting up and for several days did not enter.

sentences.zh: 上謀頗泄，世隆等以告榮。

translations.literal: The emperor's plot leaked somewhat; Shilong and the others reported it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's plot leaked somewhat, and Shilong and the others reported it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮輕帝，不謂能反。

translations.literal: Rong looked down on the emperor and did not think he could rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Rong looked down on the emperor and did not think he could rebel.

sentences.zh: 預帝謀者皆懼。

translations.literal: All who shared in the emperor's plot were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: All who shared in the emperor's plot were afraid.

sentences.zh: 二十五日旦，榮、天穆同入，其日大欲革易。

translations.literal: At dawn on the twenty-fifth Rong and Tianmu entered together; that day the great change was intended.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the twenty-fifth Rong and Tianmu entered together. That day the great change was intended.

sentences.zh: 上在明光殿東序中西面坐，榮與天穆並御床西北小床上南坐，城陽入，始一拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sat facing west in the western section of the eastern wing of the Mingguang Hall; Rong and Tianmu both sat facing south on a small couch northwest of the imperial bed; Prince of Chengyang entered and bowed once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat facing west in the western section of the eastern wing of the Mingguang Hall. Rong and Tianmu both sat facing south on a small couch northwest of the imperial bed. Prince of Chengyang entered and bowed once.

sentences.zh: 榮見光祿卿魯安等持刀從東戶入，即馳向御坐，帝拔千牛刀，手斬之，時年三十八。

translations.literal: Rong saw Director of the Imperial Household Lu An and others enter with blades from the eastern door; he immediately rushed toward the imperial seat; the emperor drew the imperial blade and cut him down with his own hand—Rong was thirty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Rong saw Director of the Imperial Household Lu An and others enter with blades from the eastern door and immediately rushed toward the imperial seat. The emperor drew the imperial blade and cut him down with his own hand. Rong was thirty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 得其手板上有數牒啟，皆左右去留人名，非其腹心，悉在出限。

translations.literal: On his hand board were found several memorials and reports—all names of those at court to be dismissed or retained; none of his trusted inner circle, all marked for removal.
translations.idiomatic: On his hand board were found several memorials and reports—all names of those at court to be dismissed or retained. None of his trusted inner circle; all were marked for removal.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豎子！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wretched brat!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wretched brat!

sentences.zh: 若過今日，便不可制。

translations.literal: If he had passed this day, he could no longer have been controlled.
translations.idiomatic: If he had passed this day, he could no longer have been controlled.

sentences.zh: 」時又天穆與榮子菩提亦就戮，於是內外喜叫，聲滿京城。

translations.literal: " At the same time Tianmu and Rong's son Puti were also executed; thereupon within and without rejoicing shouts filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " At the same time Tianmu and Rong's son Puti were also executed. Thereupon rejoicing shouts within and without filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而大赦。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 榮雖威名大振，而舉止輕脫，止以馳射為伎藝，每入朝見，更無所為，唯戲上下馬。

translations.literal: Though Rong's prestige and fame were greatly raised, his conduct was frivolous and unrestrained; he regarded only riding and shooting as his art; whenever he entered court audience he did nothing else but play at mounting and dismounting.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rong's prestige and fame were greatly raised, his conduct was frivolous and unrestrained. He regarded only riding and shooting as his art, and whenever he entered court audience he did nothing else but play at mounting and dismounting.

sentences.zh: 于西林園宴射，恆請皇后出觀，並召王公妃主，共在一堂。

translations.literal: At Xilin Garden for banquet and archery, he constantly requested the empress to come out and watch, and summoned princes, dukes, consorts, and princesses—all together in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets and archery in Xilin Garden, he always insisted the empress come out to watch, and gathered princes, dukes, imperial consorts, and princesses together in a single hall.

sentences.zh: 每見天子射中，輒自起舞叫，將相卿士，悉皆盤旋，乃至妃主婦人，亦不免隨之舉袂。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the Son of Heaven hit the target, he would himself rise dancing and shouting; generals, ministers, and officials all whirled about, and even consorts and noble women could not avoid raising their sleeves to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor's arrow found its mark, Rong would leap up dancing and shouting. Generals, ministers, and courtiers spun in circles, and even consorts and noblewomen could not help lifting their sleeves and joining in.

sentences.zh: 及酒酣耳熱，必自匡坐，唱虜歌，為《樹梨普梨》之曲。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep and the ears hot, he would himself sit upright, sing barbarian songs, and perform the tune 'Shuli Puli.'
translations.idiomatic: Once the wine had gone to his head, he would sit bolt upright and sing barbarian songs, performing the tune "Shuli Puli."

sentences.zh: 見臨淮王彧從容閒雅，愛尚風素，固令為敕勒舞。

translations.literal: Seeing Prince of Linhuai Yu at ease, refined, and elegant, loving and honoring plain simplicity, he insisted he perform the Tiele dance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Prince of Linhuai Yu's easy grace and taste for plain elegance, he ordered him to perform the Tiele dance.

sentences.zh: 日暮罷歸，便與左右聯手蹋地，唱《回波樂》而出。

translations.literal: At dusk when the gathering ended and he returned, he would link hands with those beside him, stomp the ground, and depart singing 'Huibo Le.'
translations.idiomatic: When the day's sport ended at dusk, he would link arms with his attendants, stamp the ground in rhythm, and leave singing "Huibo Le."

sentences.zh: 性甚嚴暴，慍喜無恆，弓箭刀槊，不離於手，每有瞋嫌，即行忍害，左右恆有死憂。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely harsh and violent; anger and joy had no constancy. Bow, arrows, blade, and spear never left his hand. Whenever he felt resentment, he immediately inflicted cruel harm; those beside him constantly had fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: He was ferociously violent, his moods swinging without warning. Bow, arrows, sword, and spear never left his hand, and at the slightest provocation he killed without hesitation. Those around him lived in constant dread of death.

sentences.zh: 曾欲出獵，有人訴之，披陳不已，發怒，即射殺之。

translations.literal: Once when he wished to go out hunting, someone came to plead a case and kept laying out grievances without cease. Enraged, he immediately shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as he was about to go hunting, a petitioner kept pressing his case without end. Rong flew into a rage and shot him dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 曾見沙彌重騎一馬，榮即令相觸，力窮不復能動，遂使傍人以頭相擊，死而後已。

translations.literal: Once he saw two novice monks both riding one horse. Rong immediately ordered them to charge against each other; when their strength was exhausted and neither could move, he then had those beside them strike heads together until death, and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw two novice monks sharing a single horse. Rong had them charge at each other until both collapsed from exhaustion, then ordered bystanders to bash their heads together until they were dead.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，世隆等得志，乃詔贈假黃鉞、相國、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事、晉王，加九錫，給九旒鑾輅，武賁班劍三百人，轀輬車，准晉太宰、安平獻王故事，諡曰武。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin's reign, when Shilong and the others had gotten their way, an edict posthumously awarded the ceremonial yellow axe, Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Prince of Jin, with the addition of the Nine Bestowals, granting the nine-tassel imperial carriage, three hundred guards with ceremonial swords, the imperial hearse, following the precedent of Jin's Grand Preceptor, Duke Xian of Anping, with the posthumous name Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Jiemin's reign, once Shilong and his faction had secured power, an edict posthumously ennobled Rong with the yellow battle-axe, the chancellorship, the directorship of the Masters of Writing, supreme command of all armies, and the title Prince of Jin, together with the full Nine Bestowals—the nine-tassel carriage, three hundred ceremonial sword-bearers, and the imperial hearse—on the model of Jin's Grand Preceptor, Duke Xian of Anping, with the posthumous name Wu.

sentences.zh: 又詔百官議榮配饗，司直劉季明曰：「晉王若配永安，則不能終臣節。

translations.literal: Another edict summoned the hundred officials to deliberate on Rong's paired sacrificial honors. Direct Censor Liu Jiming said: 'If the Prince of Jin were paired with Yong'an, he could not have completed the full span of a subject's loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: A further edict called on the court to decide with whom Rong should share sacrificial honors. Direct Censor Liu Jiming argued: "If the Prince of Jin were paired with Emperor Yong'an, he could not have remained a loyal subject to the end."

sentences.zh: 以此論之，無所配。

translations.literal: On this reasoning, there is no one with whom to pair.
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, there was no appropriate match at all.

sentences.zh: 」世隆作色曰：「卿合配？

translations.literal: Shilong's face changed color and he said: 'Do you think you should be paired?'
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's expression darkened. "Perhaps you think you deserve a place in the temple?"

sentences.zh: 」季明曰：「下官預在議限，據理而言，不合上心，誅翦唯命。

translations.literal: Jiming said: 'This humble official falls within the scope of deliberation. Speaking according to reason, if my words do not accord with Your Excellency's wish, execution is at your command.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiming replied: "I am among those whose views were solicited. I speak as reason dictates. If that displeases you, I submit to whatever punishment you decree."

sentences.zh: 」眾為之危，季明自若。

translations.literal: The assembly was alarmed for him; Jiming remained as if nothing were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly feared for his life, but Jiming showed not a trace of alarm.

sentences.zh: 世隆意不已，乃配享孝文廟庭。

translations.literal: Shilong's resentment did not cease, and [Rong] was assigned paired sacrifice in the court of Emperor Xiaowen's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong would not let the matter drop, and Rong was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Xiaowen's temple.

sentences.zh: 菩提位太常卿、開府儀同三司、侍中、特進。

translations.literal: Puti held the posts of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand General with seal equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: Puti held the offices of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand General with privileges equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, and Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 死時年十四。

translations.literal: When he died he was fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fourteen when he died.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，加贈司徒，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin's reign, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Steward with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Jiemin's reign, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Steward and given the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 菩提弟叉羅，武衛將軍、梁郡王。

translations.literal: Puti's younger brother Chaluo was General of the Martial Guard and Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Puti's younger brother Chaluo served as General of the Martial Guard and Prince of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously awarded Duke of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously ennobled as Duke of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 尒硃文暢

translations.literal: Er Zhu Wenchang
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhu Wenchang

sentences.zh: 尒硃文略

translations.literal: Er Zhu Wenlue
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhu Wenlue

sentences.zh: 弟文略，以兄叉羅卒無後，襲叉羅爵梁郡王。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wenlue, because elder brother Chaluo died without heirs, inherited Chaluo's title Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlue, the younger brother, inherited the title Prince of Liang Commandery after Chaluo died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 文暢事當從坐，靜帝使人往晉陽，欲拉殺之。

translations.literal: Wenchang's matter ought to have brought shared punishment by association; Emperor Jing sent men to Jinyang intending to beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang should have been punished as an accomplice; Emperor Jing sent men to Jinyang to beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 神武特加寬貸，奏免之。

translations.literal: Shenwu specially extended leniency and memorialized to exempt him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu intervened on his behalf and secured a pardon.

sentences.zh: 文略聰明俊爽，多所通習。

translations.literal: Wenlue was clever, handsome, and quick-witted, broadly versed in many skills.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlue was brilliant, handsome, and quick-witted, with wide-ranging talents.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄嘗令章永興馬上彈琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得八。

translations.literal: Qi Wencheng once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback, performing more than ten tunes; Wenlue was tried at transcribing them and got eight.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi Wencheng had Zhang Yongxing play more than ten pipa pieces on horseback and tested Wenlue by asking him to reproduce them; Wenlue got eight right.

sentences.zh: 文襄戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之！

translations.literal: Wencheng joked with him, saying: 'Clever men often do not live long—Prince of Liang Commandery, take care!'
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng teased him: "Clever men seldom live long, Prince of Liang Commandery—take care!"

sentences.zh: 」文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。

translations.literal: Wenlue replied: 'Whether my life is long or short rests entirely with Your Excellency.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenlue answered: "Whether I live long or die young is entirely in your hands, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」文襄愴然曰：「此不足慮。

translations.literal: Wencheng said sadly: 'That is nothing to worry about.'
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng said wistfully: "That is nothing to worry about."

sentences.zh: 」初，神武遣令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所陵忽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shenwu had ordered that Wenlue be forgiven ten capital offenses; relying on this he grew ever more overbearing and frequently slighted others.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu had once granted Wenlue immunity from ten capital offenses, and emboldened by this privilege he grew ever more arrogant and contemptuous of others.

sentences.zh: 齊天保末，嘗邀平秦、武興、汝南諸王至宅，供設奢麗，各有贈賄。

translations.literal: Late in Qi Tianbao, he once invited the kings of Pingqin, Wuxing, and Runan to his residence, with lavish provisions; each received gifts and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao reign of Qi, he once invited the kings of Pingqin, Wuxing, and Runan to his home, entertained them lavishly, and showered each with gifts.

sentences.zh: 諸王共假聚寶物以要之，文略弊衣而往，從奴五十人，皆駿馬侯服。

translations.literal: The kings together borrowed treasures to show off; Wenlue went in shabby clothes with fifty servants, all on fine horses in princely attire.
translations.idiomatic: The princes pooled their treasures to put on a show of wealth; Wenlue arrived in threadbare clothes with fifty attendants, every one mounted on a fine horse and dressed like a nobleman.

sentences.zh: 其豪縱不遜如此。

translations.literal: His unrestrained arrogance was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the swaggering insolence of his ways.

sentences.zh: 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭取之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin had a horse famed for seven hundred li; Wenlue wagered a fine maid against it and won the horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse said to run seven hundred li in a day; Wenlue wagered a beautiful maid against it and won the horse.

sentences.zh: 明日，平秦王使人致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。

translations.literal: The next day the Prince of Pingqin sent someone to reclaim it; Wenlue killed both the horse and the maid, placed the maid's head and horse meat in two silver vessels, and sent them as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Prince of Pingqin sent a messenger to reclaim the horse. Wenlue slaughtered both the horse and the maid, put the maid's head and the horse's flesh in two silver bowls, and sent them back as his reply.

sentences.zh: 平秦王訴之于文宣，系於京畿獄。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingqin appealed to Emperor Wenxuan; [Wenlue] was imprisoned in the capital circuit jail.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Wenlue was thrown into the capital prison.

sentences.zh: 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠倦極，便臥唱挽輓歌歌。

translations.literal: Wenlue played the pipa, blew the transverse flute, chanted songs until utterly wearied, then lay down singing dirges.
translations.idiomatic: In prison Wenlue played the pipa, blew the flute, and sang until he was exhausted, then lay down and crooned funeral dirges.

sentences.zh: 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人，曰：「不然，天子不憶我。

translations.literal: After several months he seized the guards' bow and arrows to shoot people, saying: 'Otherwise the Son of Heaven will not remember me.'
translations.idiomatic: After several months he snatched the guards' bow and arrows and shot at people, saying, "Otherwise the emperor will never think of me again."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏，遂伏法。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized; he was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the matter, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為父作佳傳，收論榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。

translations.literal: Wenlue once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold, asking him to write a fine biography of his father; Wei Shou compared Rong to Wei, Peng, Yi, and Huo—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlue once paid Wei Shou a large sum in gold to compose a flattering biography of his father—hence Wei Shou's comparison of Rong to the great ministers Wei, Peng, Yi, and Huo.

sentences.zh: 尒硃兆

translations.literal: Er Zhu Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhu Zhao

sentences.zh: 兆字萬仁，榮從子也。

translations.literal: Zhao, courtesy name Wanren, was Rong's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, courtesy name Wanren, was Er Zhurong's nephew.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，趫捷過人，數從榮遊獵，至窮岩絕澗，人所不能升降者，兆必先之。

translations.literal: From youth he excelled at mounted archery, surpassing others in agility; he often accompanied Rong on hunts. At sheer cliffs and bottomless ravines where people could not climb up or down, Zhao always went first.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was an outstanding horseman and archer, more agile than anyone around him. On Rong's hunting expeditions, wherever the terrain was sheer cliff or impassable gorge, Zhao was always the first to go.

sentences.zh: 手格猛獸，無所疑避。

translations.literal: He grappled fierce beasts with his bare hands, never hesitating or shrinking back.
translations.idiomatic: He wrestled wild beasts bare-handed, never flinching.

sentences.zh: 榮以此特加賞愛，任為爪牙。

translations.literal: Rong for this reason particularly favored and rewarded him, appointing him as his enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Rong prized him all the more for this and made him his right-hand man.

sentences.zh: 榮曾送台使，見二鹿，授兆二箭，令取供今食。

translations.literal: Rong once was seeing off an imperial envoy when he spotted two deer; he gave Zhao two arrows and told him to fetch them for the day's meal.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while seeing off an imperial envoy, Rong spotted two deer and handed Zhao two arrows, telling him to bring them back for the evening meal.

sentences.zh: 遂構火以待之。

translations.literal: He then built a fire and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao built a fire and waited.

sentences.zh: 俄而兆獲其一，榮欲誇使人，責兆不盡取，杖之五十。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao got one; Rong, wishing to impress the envoy, reproached Zhao for not taking both and flogged him fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao brought back one deer. Wanting to show off before the envoy, Rong berated him for failing to take both and had him beaten fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 榮之入洛，兆兼前鋒都督。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Zhao served concurrently as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong marched into Luoyang, Zhao served as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊即位，封潁川郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後從上党王天穆平邢杲。

translations.literal: Later he followed Shangdang Prince Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Shangdang Prince Tianmu in suppressing Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 又與賀拔勝擊斬元顥子冠受，禽之。

translations.literal: He also joined Heba Sheng in striking down and beheading Yuan Hao's son Guanshou, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought alongside Heba Sheng, killing and capturing Yuan Hao's son Guanshou.

sentences.zh: 進破安豐王延明，顥乃退走。

translations.literal: Advancing, they broke Prince of Anfeng Yanming; Hao then fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward, they routed Prince of Anfeng Yanming, and Yuan Hao fled.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，論功除車騎大將軍、儀同三司、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, merits were assessed and [Zhao] was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal in rank to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the capital, Zhao was rewarded with the posts of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, privileges equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮死，兆自汾州據晉陽。

translations.literal: When Er Zhurong died, Zhao from Fenzhou seized Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Er Zhurong's death, Zhao moved from Fenzhou and seized Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，授兆大將軍，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Zhao was granted the title Grand General and promoted to king.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Zhao was made Grand General and elevated to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 兆與世隆等定謀攻洛。

translations.literal: Zhao with Shilong and the others settled on a plan to attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao joined Shilong and the others in plotting an assault on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 兆遂輕兵倍道，掩襲京邑。

translations.literal: Zhao then led light troops by forced marches and launched a surprise assault on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then raced ahead with a light force and struck the capital by surprise.

sentences.zh: 先是，河邊人夢神謂己曰：「尒硃家欲度河，用爾作灅波津令，為之縮水脈。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man by the river dreamed a god told him: 'The Er Zhu family wishes to cross the river; they will use you as commander of Zhuobo Ford and shrink the waters for them.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man living by the river dreamed that a god told him: "The Er Zhu clan intends to cross the river. They will appoint you commander of Zhuobo Ford and make you shrink the waters for them."

sentences.zh: 」月餘，夢者死。

translations.literal: After a month and more the dreamer died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later the dreamer died.

sentences.zh: 及兆至，有行人自言知水淺處，以草往往表插而導焉，忽失其所在。

translations.literal: When Zhao arrived, a traveler claimed to know where the water was shallow; he marked the route by sticking grass here and there to guide them, then suddenly vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao arrived, a passerby claimed to know where the river was shallow and marked the way by sticking tufts of grass along the route—then vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 兆遂策馬涉度。

translations.literal: Zhao then spurred his horse and waded across.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao spurred his horse into the water and crossed.

sentences.zh: 是日暴風鼓怒，黃塵張天，騎叩宮門，宿衛乃覺。

translations.literal: That day a raging gale blew; yellow dust filled the sky; cavalry knocked on the palace gates—the palace guards only then realized [what was happening].
translations.idiomatic: That day a violent storm rose, yellow dust blotted out the sky, and horsemen were pounding on the palace gates before the guards even realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 彎弓欲射，袍撥弦，矢不得發，一時散走。

translations.literal: They bent bows to shoot, but their robes caught the strings and the arrows would not fly; in an instant all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They strung their bows to shoot, but their robes snagged the strings and the arrows would not fly; in moments the guards broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 莊帝步出雲龍門外，為兆騎所擊，幽于永寧佛寺。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang walked out beyond the Cloud Dragon Gate, was struck by Zhao's horsemen, and was confined in Yongning Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang fled on foot beyond the Cloud Dragon Gate, was overtaken by Zhao's cavalry, and imprisoned in Yongning Buddhist Temple.

sentences.zh: 兆撲殺皇子，汙辱妃嬪，縱兵虜掠。

translations.literal: Zhao beat the imperial princes to death, debauched the consorts and concubines, and let his troops plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao beat the imperial princes to death, violated the consorts and concubines, and let his soldiers loot at will.

sentences.zh: 停洛旬余，先令衛送莊帝于晉陽，兆後於河梁監閱財貨。

translations.literal: He stayed in Luoyang for more than ten days; first he sent guards to convey Emperor Zhuang to Jinyang, while Zhao himself later supervised the inspection of goods at He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Luoyong for over ten days, first sending guards to escort Emperor Xiaozhuang to Jinyang while he himself stayed behind at He Bridge to oversee the plunder.

sentences.zh: 初，兆將入洛，遣使招齊神武，欲與同舉。

translations.literal: Initially when Zhao was about to enter Luoyang, he dispatched a messenger to recruit Qi Shenwu, wishing to act together.
translations.idiomatic: Before entering Luoyang, Zhao sent a messenger to recruit Qi Shenwu, hoping to act in concert with him.

sentences.zh: 神武時為晉州刺史，謂長史孫騰曰：「臣而伐君，其逆已甚。

translations.literal: Shenwu was then Inspector of Jinyang; he said to Chief Clerk Sun Teng: 'A subject attacking his ruler—such rebellion is already extreme.'
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was then Inspector of Jinyang. He told his chief clerk Sun Teng: "For a subject to attack his sovereign is rebellion in its worst form."

sentences.zh: 我今不往，恐彼致恨，卿可往申吾意，但雲山蜀未平，不可委去。

translations.literal: 'If I do not go now, I fear they will bear a grudge. You may go and explain my intent—only say the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and I cannot leave my post.'
translations.idiomatic: "If I refuse to go, they will resent it. Go and explain my position—tell them only that the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and I cannot leave my post."

sentences.zh: 」騰乃詣兆，具申意。

translations.literal: Sun Teng then went to Zhao and fully stated his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng went to Zhao and delivered the message in full.

sentences.zh: 兆不悅，曰：「還白高兄弟，有吉夢，今行必克。

translations.literal: Zhao was displeased and said: 'Go back and tell the Gao brothers: I had an auspicious dream; this expedition is sure to succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was displeased. "Go back and tell the Gao brothers," he said, "I have had an auspicious dream. This campaign cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 吾比夢吾亡父登一高堆，堆傍地悉耕熟，唯有馬蘭草株，往往猶在，吾父顧我，令下拔之。

translations.literal: 'Recently I dreamed my late father climbed a high mound; all the land beside the mound was plowed smooth, only stalks of malan grass here and there remained. My father looked at me and told me to go down and pull them up.'
translations.idiomatic: "I dreamed my dead father stood atop a high mound. All the land around it had been plowed smooth, but here and there stalks of malan grass still stood. My father looked at me and told me to go down and pull them up."

sentences.zh: 吾手所至，無不盡出。

translations.literal: 'Wherever my hand reached, none remained unuprooted.'
translations.idiomatic: "Every stalk my hand touched came up without exception."

sentences.zh: 以此而言，往必有利。

translations.literal: 'By this token, going forth is sure to bring advantage.'
translations.idiomatic: "By that omen, this expedition is bound to succeed."

sentences.zh: 」騰還，具報之。

translations.literal: Sun Teng returned and reported it all.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng returned and reported everything Zhao had said.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「兆等倡狂，舉兵犯順，吾勢不可反事尒硃也。

translations.literal: Shenwu said: 'Zhao and his ilk are wildly reckless, raising troops in rebellion against the rightful order. Given my position I cannot in turn serve the Er Zhu clan.'
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said: "Zhao and his kind are mad with ambition, raising arms in rebellion against the throne. In my position I cannot simply submit to the Er Zhu clan."

sentences.zh: 今天子列兵河上，兆進不能度，必退還。

translations.literal: 'Now the Son of Heaven has deployed troops along the river; Zhao advancing will be unable to cross and is sure to retreat.'
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor has massed troops along the river. Zhao will not be able to cross and will have to retreat."

sentences.zh: 吾乘山東下，出其不意，此徒可一舉而禽。

translations.literal: 'I will ride down from the eastern provinces, take them by surprise—this lot can be captured in one stroke.'
translations.idiomatic: "I will sweep down from the east and catch them off guard—we can destroy them in a single blow."

sentences.zh: 」俄而兆克京師，孝莊幽縶，都督尉景從兆南行，以書報神武。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao took the capital; Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned. Commander Wei Jing followed Zhao south and sent a letter reporting to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao seized the capital and Emperor Xiaozhuang was taken prisoner. Commander Wei Jing accompanied Zhao south and wrote to inform Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武大驚，召騰，令馳驛詣兆，示以謁賀，密觀天子所在，當于路邀迎，唱大義於天下。

translations.literal: Shenwu was greatly alarmed; he summoned Teng and ordered him to ride post-haste to Zhao, show congratulations of audience, secretly observe where the Son of Heaven was, and along the way intercept and welcome him, proclaiming righteous cause to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was deeply alarmed. He summoned Sun Teng and ordered him to ride post-haste to Zhao with congratulations, secretly ascertain the emperor's whereabouts, intercept and rescue him along the road, and proclaim the righteous cause to the realm.

sentences.zh: 騰遇帝于中路，神武時率騎東轉，聞帝已度，於是西還。

translations.literal: Teng met the emperor on the road; Shenwu at the time was leading cavalry eastward—hearing the emperor had already passed, he then turned back west.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng met the emperor on the road, but by then Shenwu had already turned his cavalry east; learning the emperor had passed, he wheeled back west.

sentences.zh: 仍與兆書，具陳禍福，不宜害天子，受惡名於海內。

translations.literal: He still wrote Zhao a letter fully setting forth fortune and calamity—that he ought not harm the Son of Heaven and incur an evil name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He still wrote to Zhao, laying out the consequences in full—that he must not harm the emperor and earn the hatred of the empire.

sentences.zh: 兆怒不納，而帝遂遇弑。

translations.literal: Zhao in anger refused to accept it, and the emperor was then assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao angrily rejected the advice, and the emperor was murdered.

sentences.zh: 初，榮既死，莊帝詔河西人紇豆陵步蕃等，令襲秀容。

translations.literal: Initially after Rong died, Emperor Zhuang ordered the Hexi men Gedouling Bufan and others to attack Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, Emperor Xiaozhuang had ordered the Hexi commander Gedouling Bufan and others to attack Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 兆入洛後，步蕃兵勢甚盛，南逼晉陽。

translations.literal: After Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's army grew very strong and pressed south toward Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's forces grew formidable and pressed south toward Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 兆所以不暇留洛，回師禦之。

translations.literal: The reason Zhao could not linger in Luoyang was that he turned his army back to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: This was why Zhao could not remain in Luoyang—he had to turn back to face Bufan.

sentences.zh: 頻為步蕃所敗，於是部勒士馬，謀出山東，令人頻徵神武。

translations.literal: Repeatedly defeated by Bufan, he then regrouped troops and horses and planned to move into the eastern provinces, repeatedly sending orders summoning Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Suffering repeated defeats at Bufan's hands, Zhao regrouped his forces and planned to move into the eastern provinces, sending repeated summons to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武晉州僚屬，並勸不行。

translations.literal: Shenwu's staff in Jinyang all advised against going.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu's advisers in Jinyang all urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 神武揣其勢迫，必無他慮，決策赴之。

translations.literal: Shenwu gauged that with their position desperate they would surely have no other designs, and decided to go.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu judged that with their backs to the wall they would have no ulterior designs, and decided to go.

sentences.zh: 兆乃分三州六鎮之人，令神武統領。

translations.literal: Zhao then divided out the people of the three provinces and six garrisons and put Shenwu in command of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then assigned Shenwu command over the troops of the three provinces and six garrisons.

sentences.zh: 神武既分兵別營，乃引兵南出，避步蕃之銳。

translations.literal: Once Shenwu had split off troops into separate camps, he led his force south to avoid Bufan's sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shenwu had detached his own force into a separate camp, he marched south to avoid Bufan's main thrust.

sentences.zh: 步蕃至樂平郡，神武與兆還討，破斬之。

translations.literal: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Shenwu and Zhao turned back to attack and broke and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Shenwu and Zhao turned back, defeated him, and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 及節閔帝立，授兆使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、柱國大將軍，兼錄尚書事、大行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, Zhao was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, Grand General of the State Pillar, concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, Zhao was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, supreme commander of all armies, Grand General of the State Pillar, concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers.

sentences.zh: 又以兆為天柱大將軍，兆以是榮所終之官，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Zhao was also offered the post of Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar—the last office Rong held—but Zhao on that account firmly declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was also offered the title Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar—the last office Er Zhurong had held—but he firmly refused on that account.

sentences.zh: 尋加都督十州諸軍事，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Commander of military affairs in ten provinces and hereditary Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was further appointed commander of military affairs in ten provinces and hereditary Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武之克殷州也，兆與仲遠、度律約拒之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu captured Yingzhou, Zhao with Zhongyuan and Dulü agreed to resist him together.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu captured Yingzhou, Zhao joined Zhongyuan and Dulü in an agreement to resist him.

sentences.zh: 仲遠、度律次陽平，兆屯廣阿，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and Dulü encamped at Yangping; Zhao stationed troops at Guang'a—the host was said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and Dulü camped at Yangping while Zhao held Guang'a; their combined forces were said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 神武廣縱反間，於是兩不相信，各致猜疑。

translations.literal: Shenwu spread disinformation widely; thereupon the two sides no longer trusted each other, each growing suspicious of the other.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu flooded the camps with disinformation, and the allies lost faith in one another, each side growing suspicious of the other.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等頻使斛斯椿賀拔勝往喻之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others repeatedly sent Husichen and Hebasheng to go explain matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and his allies repeatedly sent Husichen and Hebasheng to reason with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆輕騎三百，來就仲遠，同坐幕下。

translations.literal: Zhao with three hundred light cavalry came to join Zhongyuan, and they sat together beneath the camp awning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rode in with three hundred light cavalry to meet Zhongyuan, and the two men sat together under the camp awning.

sentences.zh: 兆性粗獷，意色不平，手舞馬鞭，長嘯凝望，深疑仲遠等有變，遂趨出馳還。

translations.literal: Zhao was coarse and uncouth by nature; his expression was sullen. He whipped his riding crop in his hand, gave a long whistle and stared fixedly, deeply suspecting that Zhongyuan and the others intended treachery, and rushed out and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was coarse and wild by nature, and his face darkened. He flourished his riding crop, gave a long whistle, and stared hard into the distance, deeply convinced that Zhongyuan and his allies were plotting treachery. He bolted from the tent and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣椿、勝等追而曉譬，兆遂拘縛將還，經日放遣。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent Husichen, Hebasheng, and the others in pursuit to explain and persuade; Zhao then bound and seized them to take back, and after a day released them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent Husichen, Hebasheng, and the others in pursuit to reason with him. Zhao seized and bound them and was about to take them away, but after a day he released them.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等於是奔退。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others thereupon fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and his allies thereupon broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 神武乃進擊，兆軍大敗。

translations.literal: Shenwu then pressed the attack, and Zhao's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu then pressed the attack, and Zhao's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 兆與仲遠、度律遂相疑阻，久而不和。

translations.literal: Zhao with Zhongyuan and Dulü then mutually suspected and obstructed one another, and for a long time were not reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Zhongyuan, and Dulü grew mutually suspicious and obstructive, and remained at odds for a long time.

sentences.zh: 世隆請節閔納兆女為皇后，兆乃大喜。

translations.literal: Shilong asked Emperor Jiemin to take Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong persuaded Emperor Jiemin to take Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 世隆謀抗神武，乃降辭厚禮，喻兆赴洛。

translations.literal: Shilong plotted to resist Shenwu; he therefore used humble words and lavish gifts to persuade Zhao to come to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong plotted to resist Shenwu and sent Zhao humble words and lavish gifts to lure him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 兆與天光、度律更自信約，然後大會韓陵山。

translations.literal: Zhao with Tiangguang and Dulü renewed their pledge of trust, and then assembled in force at Hanling Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao renewed his pact of trust with Tiangguang and Dulü, then mustered their combined forces at Hanling Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，復奔晉陽。

translations.literal: They were defeated in battle and again fled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: They were defeated and again fled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，神武自鄴進討之，兆遂大掠并州，走于秀容。

translations.literal: That autumn Shenwu advanced from Ye to attack him; Zhao then plundered Bingzhou on a great scale and fled to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Shenwu marched from Ye to pursue him. Zhao plundered Bingzhou on a vast scale and fled toward Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 神武又追擊，度赤洪嶺，破之。

translations.literal: Shenwu again pursued and attacked, crossed Chihong Ridge, and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu pursued him again, crossed Chihong Ridge, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 兆竄於窮山，殺所乘馬，自縊於樹。

translations.literal: Zhao hid himself in a remote mountain, killed the horse he was riding, and hanged himself from a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled into the wild mountains, killed his mount, and hanged himself from a tree.

sentences.zh: 神武收葬之。

translations.literal: Shenwu gathered his remains and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu recovered his body and gave him a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 兆勇於戰鬥，而無將領之能。

translations.literal: Zhao was brave in battle but lacked the ability of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was brave in battle but lacked the talent of a commander.

sentences.zh: 榮雖奇其膽決，然每云：「兆不過將三千騎，多則亂矣。」

translations.literal: Rong though he admired his bold resolve, yet always said: "Zhao can command no more than three thousand cavalry; with more he falls into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Rong admired his bold resolve, yet always said, "Zhao can lead no more than three thousand cavalry—give him more and he falls apart."

sentences.zh: 兆弟智彪，節閔帝封為安定王。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Zhibiao was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding by Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Zhibiao was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding by Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 與兆俱走，神武禽之。

translations.literal: He fled together with Zhao; Shenwu captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with Zhao and was captured by Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 後死于晉陽。

translations.literal: Later he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 尒硃彥伯

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Yanbo

sentences.zh: 彥伯，榮從弟也。

translations.literal: Yanbo was Rong's younger paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was Rong's younger paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖侯真，文成時並、安二州刺史、始昌侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hou Zhen, in the time of Emperor Wen Cheng, was Inspector of the two provinces of Bing and An and Marquis of Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hou Zhen had served under Emperor Wen Cheng as Inspector of Bing and An provinces and as Marquis of Shichang.

sentences.zh: 父買珍，宣武時武衛將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Mai Zhen, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu, was General of the Martial Guard and Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mai Zhen had served under Emperor Xuanwu as General of the Martial Guard and Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 彥伯性和厚，永安中，為榮府長史。

translations.literal: Yanbo's nature was gentle and generous; in the Yong'an era he served as Chief Clerk in Rong's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was gentle and generous by nature. During the Yong'an era he served as chief clerk in Rong's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝潛嘿于龍花佛寺，彥伯敦喻往來，尤有勤款。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin was kept in secret seclusion at Longhua Buddhist Temple; Yanbo earnestly urged and guided the comings and goings, showing especial diligence and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Jiemin was held in secret at Longhua Buddhist Temple, Yanbo urged and guided the exchanges between the factions with especial diligence and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝既立，尒硃兆以己不豫謀，大為忿恚，將攻世隆。

translations.literal: Once the emperor was enthroned, Er Zhurong Zhao, because he had not been included in the plot, was greatly enraged and was about to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor was enthroned, Er Zhurong Zhao, furious that he had not been included in the plot, prepared to attack Shilong.

sentences.zh: 詔令華山王鷙慰兆，兆猶不釋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Huashan Zhi to console Zhao, but Zhao still did not relent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince Huashan Zhi to placate Zhao, but Zhao still would not be appeased.

sentences.zh: 世隆復令彥伯自往喻之，兆乃止。

translations.literal: Shilong again had Yanbo go in person to explain matters to him, and Zhao then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then sent Yanbo in person to reason with him, and Zhao desisted.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝宴彥伯于顯陽殿。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor feasted Yanbo in Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo returned, the emperor held a banquet for him in Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 時侍中源子恭、黃門郎竇瑗並侍坐。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were both in attendance seated beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Zigong and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were also in attendance.

sentences.zh: 彥伯曰：「源侍中比為都督，與臣相持於河內。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Attendant Yuan, when you lately served as area commander, you and I faced off at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Attendant Yuan, when you were area commander you and I faced each other across the field at Henei.

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，旗鼓相望，眇如天隔。

translations.literal: At that time our banners and drums faced each other, distant as heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: In those days our banners and drums faced each other across a gulf as wide as heaven.

sentences.zh: 甯期同事陛下，為今日之忻也？

translations.literal: Who could have expected that we would serve Your Majesty together and share today's joy?"
translations.idiomatic: Who could have dreamed we would serve Your Majesty together and share this day's joy?"

sentences.zh: 」子恭曰：「蒯通有言，犬吠非其主。

translations.literal: Zigong said: "Kuai Tong had a saying: a dog barks not for its own master.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong replied, "Kuai Tong once said that a dog barks not for its own master.

sentences.zh: 他日之事永安，猶今日之事陛下耳。

translations.literal: Serving Yong'an in those days is the same as serving Your Majesty today."
translations.idiomatic: Serving Emperor Yong'an then is no different from serving Your Majesty now."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「源侍中可謂有射鉤之心也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart of one who shot the hook."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart of Duke Huan's loyal archer."

sentences.zh: 」遂令二人極醉而罷。

translations.literal: He then had the two men drink until utterly drunk and dismissed the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the two men drink until they were utterly drunk and dismissed the banquet.

sentences.zh: 後封博陵郡王，位司徒公。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling Commandery and held the post of Minister Over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as Prince of Boling Commandery and appointed Minister Over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 于時炎旱，有勸彥伯解司徒者，乃上表遜位，詔許之。

translations.literal: At that time there was scorching drought; some urged Yanbo to resign the post of Minister Over the Masses, and he memorialized yielding the office; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought some urged Yanbo to step down as Minister Over the Masses. He memorialized offering his resignation, and the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 俄除儀同三司、侍中，餘如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Palace Attendant; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Palace Attendant; his other honors remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 彥伯于兄弟之中，差無過患。

translations.literal: Among the brothers Yanbo was comparatively free of serious faults.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Er Zhurong brothers, Yanbo was comparatively free of serious faults.

sentences.zh: 天光等敗于韓陵，彥伯欲領兵屯河橋，世隆不從。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Yanbo wished to lead troops to encamp at Heqiao Bridge, but Shilong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Yanbo wanted to lead troops to hold Heqiao Bridge, but Shilong refused.

sentences.zh: 及張勸等掩襲世隆，彥伯時在禁直。

translations.literal: When Zhang Quan and the others launched a surprise attack on Shilong, Yanbo was at the time on palace night duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Quan and the others launched a surprise attack on Shilong, Yanbo was on palace night duty.

sentences.zh: 長孫承業等啟陳，神武義功既振，將除尒硃。

translations.literal: Changsun Chengye and the others memorialized stating that Shenwu's righteous achievement had already risen and that the Er Zhurong clan would be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Chengye and the others reported that Shenwu's righteous cause was gaining strength and that the Er Zhurong clan would soon be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 節閔令舍人郭崇報彥伯知，彥伯狼狽出走，為人所執。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Chong to inform Yanbo; Yanbo fled in panic and was seized by others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin ordered Attendant Guo Chong to warn Yanbo, but Yanbo fled in panic and was captured.

sentences.zh: 尋與世隆同斬於閶闔門外，縣首於斛斯椿門樹，傳于神武。

translations.literal: Soon he was beheaded together with Shilong outside the Changhe Gate; their heads were hung on the tree at Husichen's gate and sent to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was beheaded together with Shilong outside the Changhe Gate. Their heads were hung on the tree at Husichen's gate and sent on to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 先是洛中謠曰：「三月末，四月初，揚灰簸土覓真珠。

translations.literal: Earlier a song in Luoyang said: "At the end of the third month, at the start of the fourth, they toss ash and sift dust seeking true pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a song in Luoyang had run, "At the end of the third month, at the start of the fourth, they toss ash and sift dust seeking true pearls.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「頭去項，腳根齊，驅上樹，不須梯。

translations.literal: " It also said: "The head leaves the neck, the feet level with the roots—drive them up a tree with no need of a ladder."
translations.idiomatic: " It also said, "The head leaves the neck, the feet level with the roots—drive them up a tree with no need of a ladder."

sentences.zh: 」至是並驗。

translations.literal: " At this time both were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " By then both prophecies had come true.

sentences.zh: 子敞。

translations.literal: His son was Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chang.

sentences.zh: 尒硃敞

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Chang
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Chang

sentences.zh: 敞字乾羅。

translations.literal: Chang's style name was Qianluo.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style name was Qianluo,

sentences.zh: 彥伯之誅，敞小，隨母養于宮中。

translations.literal: When Yanbo was executed, Chang was young and was raised in the palace with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: was still a child when Yanbo was executed. He was raised in the palace with his mother.

sentences.zh: 年十二，敞自竇走至大街，見童兒群戲，敞解所著綺羅金翠服，易衣而遁。

translations.literal: At age twelve Chang slipped out through a hole in the wall to the main street, saw children playing in a group, removed the brocade, silk, gold, and jade garments he was wearing, exchanged clothes, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he slipped through a hole in the wall to the main street, saw children playing together, stripped off his brocade and jeweled garments, traded clothes with one of them, and fled.

sentences.zh: 追騎至，不識敞，便執綺衣兒。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen arrived, did not recognize Chang, and seized the child in brocade clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers arrived, failed to recognize Chang, and seized the child in brocade instead.

sentences.zh: 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是免。

translations.literal: When interrogation showed it was not he, and as the day had already grown dark, he thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation soon showed they had the wrong boy, and by then night had fallen, so Chang escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼，踞胡床坐，敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於復壁之中。

translations.literal: He then entered a village, saw an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding camp chair, bowed twice and begged for mercy; the Changsun woman pitied him and hid him inside a hidden wall compartment.
translations.idiomatic: He came to a village and found an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding chair. He bowed and begged for mercy. She took pity on him and hid him in a secret compartment behind the wall.

sentences.zh: 購之愈急，追且至，長孫氏資而遣之。

translations.literal: The reward for his capture grew ever more urgent and pursuers were about to arrive; the Changsun woman supplied him with funds and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The reward for his capture grew ever more urgent and pursuers were closing in, so the Changsun woman gave him money and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩高山。

translations.literal: He then pretended to be a Daoist priest, changed his name, and hid on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He then posed as a Daoist priest, changed his name, and hid on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 略涉經史。

translations.literal: He lightly studied the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He read somewhat in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 數年間，人頗異之。

translations.literal: Within a few years people found him rather unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years people found him rather unusual.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨坐岩石下，泫然歎曰：「吾豈終此乎！

translations.literal: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed: "Am I to end like this!
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed, "Am I to end my days like this?

sentences.zh: 伍子胥獨何人也？

translations.literal: Was Wu Zixu alone in what kind of man he was?"
translations.idiomatic: What made Wu Zixu so special?"

sentences.zh: 」乃奔長安。

translations.literal: " He then fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周文帝見而禮之，拜行台郎中、靈壽縣伯。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and treated him with courtesy, appointing him Gentleman of the Mobile Headquarters and Baron of Lingshou County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou received him with honor and appointed him Gentleman of the Mobile Headquarters and Baron of Lingshou County.

sentences.zh: 保定中，遷開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was transferred to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with the Opening of a Government Office and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with the Opening of a Government Office and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 後為膠州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 迎長孫氏至其第，置於家，厚資給之。

translations.literal: He welcomed the Changsun woman to his residence, installed her in his household, and generously supplied her needs.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the Changsun woman to his home, installed her in his household, and provided for her generously.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，改封邊城郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Chang's fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Chang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Biancheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。

translations.literal: When the Qian'an barbarians rebelled, he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qian'an tribes rebelled, he was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 師旋，拜金州總管，政號嚴明，吏人懼之。

translations.literal: When his army returned, he was appointed Area Commander of Jinzhou; his governance was strict and clear, and officials and commoners feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When his army returned, he was appointed area commander of Jinzhou. His governance was strict and clear, and officials and commoners feared him.

sentences.zh: 後以年老乞骸骨，賜二馬輅車歸河內，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later, because of old age he requested retirement; he was granted a two-horse carriage and returned to Henei, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing old age, he requested retirement. He was granted a two-horse carriage, returned to Henei, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尒硃仲遠

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Zhongyuan
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Zhongyuan

sentences.zh: 仲遠，彥伯弟也。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was Yanbo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was Yanbo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 明帝末年，尒硃榮兵威稍盛，諸有啟謁，率多見從。

translations.literal: In the final years of Emperor Ming, Er Zhurong's military prestige gradually grew strong; petitions and requests were for the most part granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Emperor Ming, Er Zhurong's military prestige grew steadily, and most petitions submitted in his name were granted.

sentences.zh: 而仲遠摹寫榮書，又刻榮印，與尚書令吏，通為奸詐。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan copied Rong's handwriting, also carved Rong's seal, and together with clerks of the Masters of Writing engaged in fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan copied Rong's handwriting, carved a seal in Rong's name, and together with clerks of the Masters of Writing engaged in fraud.

sentences.zh: 造榮啟表，請人為官，大得財貨，以資酒色。

translations.literal: He forged memorials and reports in Rong's name, soliciting appointments for others, and greatly obtained wealth and goods to support wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: He forged memorials in Rong's name to sell offices, amassed great wealth, and spent it on wine and women.

sentences.zh: 落魄無行業。

translations.literal: He was dissolute and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was dissolute and without proper occupation.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊即位，封清河公、徐州刺史，兼尚書左僕射、三徐大行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe, appointed Inspector of Xuzhou, and concurrently made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over the Three Xus.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zhongyuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe, appointed Inspector of Xuzhou, and concurrently made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over the Three Xus.

sentences.zh: 尋進督三徐諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Supervisor of military affairs in the Three Xus.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was further appointed supervisor of military affairs in the Three Xus.

sentences.zh: 仲遠上言：「竊見比來行台采募者，皆得權立中正，在軍定第，斟酌授官。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan memorialized: "I have observed that lately those recruiting troops under mobile headquarters have all been permitted to appoint arbiters of pedigree on their own authority, fix ranks within the army, and grant offices at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan memorialized, "I observe that lately recruiting commissioners have all been permitted to appoint arbiters of pedigree on their own authority, fix ranks within the army, and grant offices at discretion.

sentences.zh: 今求兼置，權濟軍要。

translations.literal: I now request to be granted the same concurrently, as a temporary measure to meet military needs.
translations.idiomatic: I now request the same authority as a temporary measure to meet military needs.

sentences.zh: 若立第亦爽，關京之日，任有司裁奪」。

translations.literal: If the ranks I assign prove unsatisfactory, on the day matters reach the capital let the proper offices revise and decide."
translations.idiomatic: If the ranks I assign prove unsatisfactory, when matters reach the capital let the proper offices revise them."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 於是隨情補授，肆意聚斂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed offices at whim and plundered without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sold offices at whim and plundered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮死，仲遠勒其部眾，來向京師。

translations.literal: When Er Zhurong died, Zhongyuan drove his troops and came toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Er Zhurong died, Zhongyuan marched his troops toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 節閔立，進爵彭城王，加大將軍，又兼尚書令，鎮大梁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, Zhongyuan was advanced to Prince of Pengcheng, given the title Grand General, and concurrently made Director of the Masters of Writing, stationed at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, Zhongyuan was promoted to Prince of Pengcheng and Grand General, concurrently appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, and stationed at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣使請准朝式，在軍鳴騶。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and have outriders announce his approach while in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and have outriders announce his approach even while in the field.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝覽啟，笑而許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin read the memorial, laughed, and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin read the memorial, laughed, and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 其肆情如此。

translations.literal: His willfulness was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 復進督東道諸軍事、本將軍、袞州刺史，余如故。

translations.literal: He was further made Supervisor of military affairs on the Eastern Route, retained his original generalship, and appointed Inspector of Yanzhou; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed supervisor of military affairs on the Eastern Route and Inspector of Yanzhou while retaining his original generalship; his other honors remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 仲遠天性貪暴，心如峻壑。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature; his heart was like a steep ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature, with a heart as deep and treacherous as a ravine.

sentences.zh: 大宗富族，誣之以反，沒其家口，簿籍財物，皆以入己。

translations.literal: Great clans and wealthy families he falsely accused of rebellion, confiscated their households, and recorded their goods and property—all entered his own possession.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely accused great clans and wealthy families of rebellion, confiscated their households, and recorded their goods and property—all for his own gain.

sentences.zh: 丈夫死者，投之河流，如此者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Men who died were cast into the river; such cases were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The men he killed were cast into the river; such cases were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 諸將婦有美色者，莫不被其淫亂。

translations.literal: Among the wives of the various generals, those of beautiful appearance none escaped his debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: None of the generals' wives who were beautiful escaped his debauchery.

sentences.zh: 自滎陽以東，輸稅悉入其軍，不送京師。

translations.literal: From Xingyang eastward, all tax deliveries went entirely into his army and were not sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingyang eastward, all tax deliveries went into his army and never reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 時天光控關右，仲遠在大梁，兆據并州，世隆居京邑，各自專恣，權強莫此。

translations.literal: At the time Tiangguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan was at Daliang, Zhao held Bingzhou, and Shilong resided in the capital region; each acted with arbitrary power on his own—nowhere was authority so strong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tiangguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan held Daliang, Zhao held Bingzhou, and Shilong dominated the capital. Each ruled his domain with arbitrary power, and nowhere was authority stronger.

sentences.zh: 所在並以貪虐為事，於是四方解體。

translations.literal: Everywhere they made greed and cruelty their business, and the realm thereby fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere they ruled through greed and cruelty, and the realm began to fall apart.

sentences.zh: 又加太宰，解大行台。

translations.literal: He was further given the title Grand Preceptor and relieved of the Grand Commissioner with Full Powers.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Grand Preceptor and relieved of his post as Grand Commissioner with Full Powers.

sentences.zh: 仲遠專恣尤劇，方之彥伯、世隆，最為無禮。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's arbitrary power was especially extreme; compared with Yanbo and Shilong, he was the most insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's arrogance was especially extreme. Compared with Yanbo and Shilong, he was the most insolent of all.

sentences.zh: 東南牧守，下至人俗，比之豺狼，特為患苦。

translations.literal: The governors and prefects of the southeast, down to the common people, compared him to wolves and jackals and found him a special source of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: From the governors and prefects of the southeast down to the common people, all compared him to wolves and jackals and found him a special source of misery.

sentences.zh: 後移屯東郡，率眾與度律等拒齊神武。

translations.literal: Later he shifted his encampment to Dong Commandery, led his troops together with Dulü and the others to resist Shenwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he shifted his camp to Dong Commandery and led his troops with Dulü and others to resist Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 尒硃兆領騎數千自晉陽來會。

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Zhao led several thousand cavalry from Jinyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Zhao led several thousand cavalry from Jinyang to join the alliance.

sentences.zh: 軍次陽平，神武縱以間說，仲遠等迭相猜貳，狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yangping, Shenwu spread disinformation freely; Zhongyuan and the others grew mutually suspicious in turn and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yangping, Shenwu flooded the camps with disinformation. Zhongyuan and his allies grew mutually suspicious and fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，復與天光等於韓陵戰敗，南走。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, he was again defeated together with Tiangguang and the others at Hanling and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he was defeated again with Tiangguang and the others at Hanling and fled south.

sentences.zh: 尋乃奔梁，死於江南。

translations.literal: Soon he fled to Liang and died in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled to Liang and died in the south.

sentences.zh: 尒硃世隆

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Shilong
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Shilong

sentences.zh: 世隆，字榮宗，仲遠弟也。

translations.literal: Shilong, style name Rongzong, was Zhongyuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, whose style name was Rongzong, was Zhongyuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 明帝末，兼直閣，加前將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ming's reign he concurrently served in the Direct Attendance Office and was given the additional title of General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Ming's reign he served in the Direct Attendance Office and was given the additional title of General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮表請入朝，靈太后惡之，令世隆詣晉陽慰喻榮。
