translations.literal: Er Zhurong memorialized requesting to enter court; Empress Dowager Ling detested this and ordered Shilong to go to Jinyang to console and persuade Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Er Zhurong memorialized requesting to enter court, Empress Dowager Ling detested the idea and ordered Shilong to go to Jinyang to placate Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮因欲留之，世隆曰：「朝廷疑兄，故令世隆來。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon wished to detain him. Shilong said: "The court suspects my elder brother, and therefore sent Shilong here.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to detain him. Shilong said, "The court suspects you, elder brother—that is why they sent me.

sentences.zh: 今遂住，便有內備，非計之善。

translations.literal: If I now stay, there will at once be internal precautions—this is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: If I stay now, the court will take internal precautions at once. That is no good plan."

sentences.zh: 」榮乃遣入。

translations.literal: " Rong then sent him back to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong then sent him back to court.

sentences.zh: 榮舉兵南出，世隆遂走，會榮於上黨。

translations.literal: When Rong raised troops and marched south, Shilong fled and joined Rong at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong raised troops and marched south, Shilong fled to join him at Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之立，世隆預其謀，封樂平郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Shilong took part in the plot and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Shilong took part in the plot and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元顥逼大梁，詔為前將軍、都督，鎮武牢。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang, an edict appointed Shilong General of the Vanguard and area commander, stationed at Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang, Shilong was appointed General of the Vanguard and area commander and stationed at Wulao.

sentences.zh: 顥既克滎陽，世隆懼而遁還，莊帝倉卒北巡。

translations.literal: Once Hao had captured Xingyang, Shilong fled in fear; Emperor Zhuang made a hurried northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao captured Xingyang, Shilong fled in fear and Emperor Zhuang made a hurried flight north.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還宮，除尚書左僕射，攝選。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and given charge of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Shilong was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and given charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之將圖尒硃榮，每屏人言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was about to plot against Er Zhurong, he always dismissed attendants before speaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was plotting against Er Zhurong, he always dismissed attendants before speaking.

sentences.zh: 世隆懼變，乃為匿名書，自榜其門曰：「天子與侍中楊侃、黃門高道穆等為計，欲殺天柱。

translations.literal: Shilong feared a coup and therefore wrote an anonymous letter, posting it on his own gate: "The Son of Heaven with Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Yellow Gate Gentleman Gao Daomu, and others are plotting to kill the Heavenly Pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong feared a coup and wrote an anonymous letter, which he posted on his own gate: "The emperor, Palace Attendant Yang Kan, Yellow Gate Gentleman Gao Daomu, and others are plotting to kill the Heavenly Pillar.

sentences.zh: 」還復自以此書與榮妻北鄉郡公主，並以呈榮，勸其不入。

translations.literal: " He then also gave this letter himself to Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang Commandery, and presented it to Rong as well, urging him not to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave the same letter to Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang Commandery, and presented it to Rong as well, urging him not to enter court.

sentences.zh: 榮毀書唾地曰：「世隆無膽，誰敢生心！

translations.literal: Rong tore up the letter and spat on the ground, saying: "Shilong has no courage—who would dare harbor such a thought!
translations.idiomatic: Rong tore up the letter and spat on the ground. "Shilong has no courage—who would dare plot against me?

sentences.zh: 」世隆又勸其速發。

translations.literal: " Shilong again urged him to set out quickly.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilong again urged him to set out quickly.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「何忽忽？

translations.literal: Rong said: "Why so hurried?
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Why so hurried?

sentences.zh: 」皆不見從。

translations.literal: " None of his advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " None of his advice was heeded.

sentences.zh: 榮死，世隆奉榮妻，燒西陽門夜走。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, burned the Xiyang Gate, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, burned the Xiyang Gate, and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 北次河橋，殺武衛將軍奚毅，率眾還戰大夏門外。

translations.literal: He halted north at Heqiao Bridge, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and led his troops back to fight outside the Daxia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He halted north at Heqiao Bridge, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and led his troops back to fight outside the Daxia Gate.

sentences.zh: 及李苗燒絕河梁，世隆乃北遁。

translations.literal: When Li Miao burned and cut off the river bridge, Shilong then fled north.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Miao burned and destroyed the river bridge, Shilong fled north.

sentences.zh: 攻建州克之，盡殺人以肆其忿。

translations.literal: He attacked Jianzhou, captured it, and killed everyone to vent his rage.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Jianzhou, captured it, and slaughtered the population to vent his rage.

sentences.zh: 至長子，與度律等共推長廣王曄為主。

translations.literal: When he reached Changzi, he together with Dulü and the others jointly raised Prince Changguang Ye as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzi he joined Dulü and the others in raising Prince Changguang Ye as their leader.

sentences.zh: 曄小名盆子，聞者皆以為事類赤眉。

translations.literal: Ye's childhood name was Penzi; those who heard of it all thought the affair resembled the Red Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's childhood name was Penzi, and those who heard of it all thought the affair resembled the Red Eyebrows rebellion.

sentences.zh: 曄以世隆為尚書令，封樂平郡王，加太傅，行司州牧，會兆于河陽。

translations.literal: Ye appointed Shilong Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed him as Prince of Leping Commandery, gave him the additional title of Grand Tutor and acting Governor of Sizhou, and joined Zhao at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye appointed Shilong Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed him as Prince of Leping Commandery, made him Grand Tutor and acting Governor of Sizhou, and joined Zhao at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 兆既平京邑，讓世隆曰：「叔父在朝多時，耳目應廣，如何令天柱受禍？

translations.literal: Once Zhao had pacified the capital region, he reproached Shilong: "Uncle, you were at court for a long time and your sources of information should have been broad—how could you let the Heavenly Pillar suffer disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao had pacified the capital, he reproached Shilong: "Uncle, you were at court for years and should have heard everything—how could you let the Heavenly Pillar come to harm?

sentences.zh: 」按劍嗔目，詞色甚厲。

translations.literal: " He gripped his sword and glared; his words and expression were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: " He gripped his sword and glared, his words and expression fierce.

sentences.zh: 世隆遜辭拜謝，然後得已，而深恨之。

translations.literal: Shilong used humble words and bowed in apology; only then was Zhao appeased, but Shilong deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong bowed and apologized humbly, and only then was Zhao appeased—but Shilong deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 時仲遠亦自滑台入京。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai.

sentences.zh: 世隆與兄弟密謀，慮元曄母幹豫朝政，伺其母衛氏出行，遣數十騎如劫賊，於京巷殺之。

translations.literal: Shilong and his brothers plotted in secret, fearing that Yuan Ye's mother would interfere in court affairs; watching for when his mother, Lady Wei, went out, they sent several dozen horsemen like bandits and killed her in a capital lane.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and his brothers plotted in secret, fearing that Yuan Ye's mother would interfere in court affairs. When Lady Wei went out, they sent several dozen horsemen disguised as bandits and killed her in a capital lane.

sentences.zh: 公私驚愕，莫識所由。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners alike were shocked; none knew who was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were shocked, and none knew who was responsible.

sentences.zh: 尋縣榜，以千萬錢募賊。

translations.literal: Soon a public notice was posted offering ten million cash to capture the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a public notice was posted offering ten million cash to capture the killers.

sentences.zh: 百姓知之，莫不喪氣。

translations.literal: When the common people learned of it, none failed to lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the people learned who was responsible, all lost heart.

sentences.zh: 尋又以曄疏遠，欲推立節閔帝。

translations.literal: Soon, because Ye was distant and remote, they wished to raise Emperor Jiemin instead.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, finding Ye unsuitable, they wished to raise Emperor Jiemin instead.

sentences.zh: 而度律意在南陽王，乃曰：「廣陵不言，何以主天下？

translations.literal: But Dulü favored the Prince of Nanyang and therefore said: "If the Prince of Guangling does not speak, how can he rule the realm?
translations.idiomatic: But Dulü favored the Prince of Nanyang and said, "If the Prince of Guangling cannot speak, how can he rule the realm?

sentences.zh: 」後知能語，遂行廢立。

translations.literal: " Later they learned he could speak, and then carried out the deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: " Later they learned he could speak, and then carried out the deposition and enthronement.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆之為僕射，尚書文簿，在家省閱。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shilong served as Vice Director, he reviewed the Masters of Writing documents and registers at home.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shilong served as Vice Director, he reviewed the Masters of Writing documents and registers at home.

sentences.zh: 性聰解，又畏榮，深自克勉，留心几案，傍接賓客，遂有解了之名。

translations.literal: He was intelligent and quick to understand; he also feared Rong, deeply restrained himself, attended closely to his desk work, and received guests on the side, and thereby gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He was intelligent and quick to understand. He also feared Rong, so he disciplined himself strictly, attended closely to his desk work, and received guests on the side, and thereby gained a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 榮死之後，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: After Rong died, he had nothing left to fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong died, he had nothing left to fear.

sentences.zh: 及為令，常使尚書郎宋游道、邢昕在其宅聽事，東西別座，受納訴訟，稱命施行。

translations.literal: Once he became Director, he regularly had Masters of Writing Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin hold court at his residence, seated separately east and west, receiving and hearing lawsuits and issuing orders in his name.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became Director, he regularly had Masters of Writing Gentlemen Song Youdao and Xing Xin hold court at his residence, seated separately east and west, hearing lawsuits and issuing orders in his name.

sentences.zh: 既總朝政，生殺自由，公行淫泆，信任群小，隨情與奪。

translations.literal: Once he controlled court affairs, he held life and death at his own discretion, openly indulged in debauchery, trusted petty men, and granted or seized at whim.
translations.idiomatic: Once he controlled court affairs, he held life and death at his own discretion, openly indulged in debauchery, trusted petty men, and granted or seized at whim.

sentences.zh: 又兄弟群從，各擁強兵，割剝四海，極其貪虐。

translations.literal: Moreover, the brothers and their clan kin each held strong armies, plundered the realm, and carried greed and cruelty to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the brothers and their clan kin each held strong armies, plundered the realm, and carried greed and cruelty to the extreme.

sentences.zh: 奸諂蛆酷，多見信用；

translations.literal: Flatterers and cruel schemers were largely trusted;
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers and cruel schemers were largely trusted;

sentences.zh: 溫良名士，罕豫腹心。

translations.literal: gentle and worthy scholars were rarely admitted to his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: while gentle and worthy scholars were rarely admitted to his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 於是天下之人，莫不厭毒。

translations.literal: Thereupon none under heaven failed to loathe and detest them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people of the realm loathed and detested them.

sentences.zh: 世隆尋讓太傅。

translations.literal: Shilong soon resigned the post of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong soon resigned as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 節閔特置儀同三師之官，位次上公之下，以世隆為之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin specially established the office of the Three Masters for Glorious Happiness, ranking below the highest dukes, and appointed Shilong to it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin specially established the office of the Three Masters for Glorious Happiness, ranking below the highest dukes, and appointed Shilong to it.

sentences.zh: 贈其父買珍相國、錄尚書事、大司馬。

translations.literal: His father Mai Zhen was posthumously given the titles of Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mai Zhen was posthumously given the titles of Chancellor of State, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起義兵，仲遠、度律等愚贛恃強，不以為慮，而世隆獨深憂恐。

translations.literal: When Shenwu of Qi raised the righteous army, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and the others were dull and arrogant, trusting in their strength and giving it no thought, but Shilong alone was deeply worried and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu raised the righteous army, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and the others were dull and arrogant, trusting in their strength and giving it no thought, but Shilong alone was deeply worried and afraid.

sentences.zh: 及天光等敗于韓陵，世隆請赦天下，節閔不許。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Shilong requested a general amnesty; Emperor Jiemin did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Shilong requested a general amnesty, but Emperor Jiemin refused.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿既據河橋，盡殺世隆黨附，令行台長孫承業詣闕奏狀，掩執世隆及兄彥伯，俱斬之。

translations.literal: Once Husichen had seized Heqiao Bridge, he killed all of Shilong's partisans, had Mobile Headquarters chief Changsun Chengye go to the palace to report the situation, and seized Shilong and his elder brother Yanbo by surprise and beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: Once Husichen had seized Heqiao Bridge, he killed all of Shilong's partisans, sent Mobile Headquarters chief Changsun Chengye to the palace to report the situation, and seized Shilong and his elder brother Yanbo by surprise and beheaded them both.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆曾與吏部尚書元世俊握槊，忽聞局上詨然有聲，一局子盡倒立，世隆甚惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shilong had been playing pitch-pot with Yuan Shijun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, when suddenly a loud crack was heard on the board and every piece stood on end; Shilong found this very ominous.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shilong had been playing pitch-pot with Yuan Shijun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, when suddenly a loud crack was heard on the board and every piece stood on end. Shilong found this very ominous.

sentences.zh: 又曾晝寢，其妻奚氏忽見一人持世隆首去。

translations.literal: On another occasion, while he was napping by day, his wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while he was napping by day, his wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head.

sentences.zh: 奚氏驚，就視，而世隆寢如故。

translations.literal: Lady Xi was startled and went to look, but Shilong was sleeping as before.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi was startled and went to look, but Shilong was sleeping as before.

sentences.zh: 既覺，謂妻曰：「向夢人斷我頭持去，意殊不適。

translations.literal: When he awoke, he said to his wife: "Just now I dreamed that a man cut off my head and carried it away—I feel very ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke, he said to his wife, "I just dreamed that a man cut off my head and carried it away. I feel very ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 」又此年正月晦日，令、僕並不上省，西門不開。

translations.literal: " Moreover, on the last day of the first month that year, the Director and Vice Directors all did not attend the ministry, and the west gate was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, on the last day of the first month that year, the Director and Vice Directors all stayed away from the ministry, and the west gate was not opened.

sentences.zh: 忽有河內太守田帖家奴，告省門亭長云：「今旦為令王借車牛一乘，終日于洛濱遊觀。

translations.literal: Suddenly a slave of Tian Tie, Inspector of Henei, reported to the gate captain of the ministry: "This morning I borrowed a cart and ox for Director Wang, and spent the whole day sightseeing along the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a slave of Tian Tie, Inspector of Henei, reported to the ministry gate captain: "This morning I borrowed a cart and ox for Director Wang, and spent the whole day sightseeing along the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 至晚，王還省，將車出東掖門，始覺車上無褥，請為記識。

translations.literal: By evening Wang returned to the ministry and was about to drive the cart out the East Side Gate when he noticed there was no cushion on the cart and asked that this be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: By evening Wang returned to the ministry and was about to drive the cart out the East Side Gate when he noticed there was no cushion on the cart and asked that this be recorded.

sentences.zh: 」亭長以令僕不上，西門不開，無跡入者。

translations.literal: " The gate captain replied that the Director and Vice Directors had not attended, the west gate had not been opened, and there was no trace of anyone entering.
translations.idiomatic: " The gate captain replied that the Director and Vice Directors had not attended, the west gate had not been opened, and there was no trace of anyone entering.

sentences.zh: 此奴固陳不已，公文列訴。

translations.literal: The slave persisted in his account without cease, and an official document was filed as a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The slave persisted in his account, and an official complaint was filed.

sentences.zh: 尚書都令史謝遠疑，謂妄有假借，白世隆，付曹推驗。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing Xie Yuanyi was suspicious, believing the account a false borrowing, reported it to Shilong, and handed it to the bureau for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing Xie Yuanyi was suspicious, believing the account a fabrication, reported it to Shilong, and handed it to the bureau for investigation.

sentences.zh: 時都官郎中穆子容究之。

translations.literal: At the time Gentleman of the Bureau of Justice Mu Zirong investigated the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Bureau of Justice Mu Zirong investigated the matter.

sentences.zh: 奴言，初來時，至司空府西，欲向省。

translations.literal: The slave said that when he first arrived, he reached the west of the Minister of Works' office and was heading toward the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The slave said that when he first arrived, he reached the west of the Minister of Works' office and was heading toward the ministry.

sentences.zh: 令王嫌遲，遣催車。

translations.literal: Director Wang thought him slow and sent someone to hurry the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang thought him slow and sent someone to hurry the cart.

sentences.zh: 車入，到省西門，王嫌牛小，系于關下槐樹，更將一青牛駕車。

translations.literal: The cart entered and reached the west gate of the ministry; Wang thought the ox too small, tied it to the locust tree beneath the gate, and had a black ox harnessed to the cart instead.
translations.idiomatic: The cart entered and reached the west gate of the ministry. Wang thought the ox too small, tied it to the locust tree beneath the gate, and had a black ox harnessed to the cart instead.

sentences.zh: 令王著白紗、高頂帽，短小、黑色，儐從皆裙襦袴褶，握板，不似常時服章。

translations.literal: Director Wang wore white gauze and a high-peaked cap; he was short and dark. His attendants all wore skirts, jackets, and trousers, holding tablets—not like their usual dress and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang wore white gauze and a high-peaked cap. He was short and dark. His attendants all wore skirts, jackets, and trousers and held tablets—not like their usual dress and insignia.

sentences.zh: 遂遣一吏將奴送入省中査事東閣內，東廂第一屋中。

translations.literal: He then sent an official to escort the slave into the ministry, to the first room in the east wing of the Eastern Investigation Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an official to escort the slave into the ministry, to the first room in the east wing of the Eastern Investigation Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其屋先常閉。

translations.literal: That room was normally kept closed.
translations.idiomatic: That room was normally kept closed.

sentences.zh: 奴雲，入此屋中有板床，床上無席，大有塵土，兼有甕米。

translations.literal: The slave said that inside the room there was a plank bed with no mat, much dust, and also a jar of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The slave said that inside the room there was a plank bed with no mat, much dust, and also a jar of rice.

sentences.zh: 奴拂床坐，兼畫地戲，甕中米亦握看之。

translations.literal: The slave dusted the bed and sat, also drew on the ground for amusement, and took the rice from the jar in his hand to look at it.
translations.idiomatic: The slave dusted the bed and sat down, drew on the ground for amusement, and took the rice from the jar in his hand to look at it.

sentences.zh: 子容與謝遠看之，閉極久，全無開跡。

translations.literal: Zirong and Yuanyi went to look; the room had been closed for a very long time and showed no trace of having been opened.
translations.idiomatic: Zirong and Yuanyi went to look. The room had been closed for a very long time and showed no trace of having been opened.

sentences.zh: 及入，狀皆符同。

translations.literal: When they entered, everything matched the account.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered, everything matched the slave's account.

sentences.zh: 具以此對世隆。

translations.literal: They reported all of this to Shilong in full.
translations.idiomatic: They reported all of this to Shilong in full.

sentences.zh: 世隆悵然，意以為惡。

translations.literal: Shilong was despondent and took it as an evil omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was despondent and took it as an evil omen.

sentences.zh: 未幾見誅。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed.

sentences.zh: 世隆弟世承，莊帝時位侍中，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: Shilong's younger brother Shicheng, in the time of Emperor Zhuang, held the post of Palace Attendant and concurrently served as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's younger brother Shicheng served under Emperor Zhuang as Palace Attendant and concurrently as Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 人才猥劣，備員而已。

translations.literal: His talent was coarse and inferior; he was merely a placeholder.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was coarse and inferior; he was merely a placeholder.

sentences.zh: 及元顥內逼，世承守轘轅，為顥所禽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Shicheng defended Huanyuan and was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Shicheng defended Huanyuan and was captured by Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥讓而臠之。

translations.literal: Hao rebuked him and had him cut to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Hao rebuked him and had him cut to pieces.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，贈司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Shicheng was posthumously given the title Minister Over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Shicheng was posthumously given the title Minister Over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 世承弟弼，字輔伯，節閔帝時，封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Shicheng's younger brother Bi, style name Fubo, in the time of Emperor Jiemin was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng's younger brother Bi, whose style name was Fubo, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery under Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 尋為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之敗，欲奔梁，數日，與左右割臂為約。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Hanling he wished to flee to Liang; after several days he cut his arm with his attendants as a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling he wished to flee to Liang. After several days he cut his arm with his attendants as a blood oath.

sentences.zh: 弼帳下都督馮紹隆為弼信待，乃說弼曰：「今方同契闊，宜當心瀝血，示眾以信。

translations.literal: Bi's camp commander Feng Shaolong, whom Bi trusted and favored, then persuaded Bi: "Now that we share life and death together, you ought to cut open your heart and pour out blood to show the troops your sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's camp commander Feng Shaolong, whom Bi trusted and favored, persuaded him: "Now that we share life and death together, you ought to cut open your heart and pour out blood to show the troops your sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」弼從之。

translations.literal: " Bi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi agreed.

sentences.zh: 大集部下，弼乃踞胡床，令紹隆持刀披心。

translations.literal: He gathered his subordinates in force; Bi then sat on a folding camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered his subordinates in force. Bi then sat on a folding camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.

sentences.zh: 紹隆因推刃殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Shaolong thereupon drove the blade in and killed him, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolong drove the blade in and killed him, then sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尒硃度律

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Dulü
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Dulü

sentences.zh: 度律，榮從父弟也，鄙樸少言。

translations.literal: Dulü was Rong's younger paternal cousin; he was rustic and plain and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü was Rong's younger paternal cousin. He was rustic and plain and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封樂鄉縣伯。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lexiang County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lexiang County.

sentences.zh: 榮死，與世隆赴晉陽。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Dulü went with Shilong to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Dulü went with Shilong to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄之立，以度律為太尉公、四面大都督，封常山王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Dulü was appointed Grand Marshal and Supreme Commander on All Four Fronts and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Dulü was appointed Grand Marshal and supreme commander on all four fronts and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 與尒硃兆入洛。

translations.literal: He entered Luoyang together with Er Zhurong Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang together with Er Zhurong Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆遷晉陽，留度律鎮京師。

translations.literal: Zhao moved to Jinyang and left Dulü to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao moved to Jinyang and left Dulü to garrison the capital.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝時，為使持節、侍中、大將軍、太尉公，兼尚書令、東北道行台，與仲遠出拒義旗。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Jiemin he held the posts of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Grand Marshal, concurrently serving as Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers on the Northeastern Route, and marched out with Zhongyuan to resist the righteous banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin he held the posts of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Grand Marshal, concurrently serving as Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers on the Northeastern Route, and marched out with Zhongyuan to resist Shenwu's righteous army.

sentences.zh: 齊神武間之，與尒硃兆遂相疑貳，自敗而還。

translations.literal: Shenwu of Qi spread disinformation, and Dulü with Er Zhurong Zhao grew mutually suspicious; he was defeated and returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu spread disinformation, and Dulü and Er Zhurong Zhao grew mutually suspicious. Dulü was defeated and retreated.

sentences.zh: 度律雖在軍戎，聚斂無厭，所經為百姓患毒。

translations.literal: Though Dulü was on campaign, he plundered without satiety; wherever he passed he became a scourge to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dulü was on campaign, he plundered without restraint, and wherever he passed he became a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 其母山氏聞度律敗，遂恚憤發病。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Shan, upon hearing of Dulü's defeat, fell ill with rage and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Shan, upon hearing of Dulü's defeat, fell ill with rage and indignation.

sentences.zh: 及至，母責之曰：「汝荷國恩，無狀而反，我何忍見他屠戮汝也！

translations.literal: When he arrived, his mother rebuked him: "You received the state's grace yet rebelled without cause—how could I bear to see others slaughter you!
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, his mother rebuked him: "You received the state's grace yet rebelled without cause—how could I bear to watch others slaughter you!

sentences.zh: 」言終而卒，時人怪異之。

translations.literal: " When she finished speaking she died; people of the time found this strange and uncanny.
translations.idiomatic: " When she finished speaking she died. People of the time found this strange and uncanny.

sentences.zh: 後韓陵之敗，斛斯椿先據河橋，遂西走氵壘波津，為人執送。

translations.literal: Later, after the defeat at Hanling, Husichen had already seized Heqiao Bridge; Dulü fled west to Leibo Ford and was seized and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after the defeat at Hanling, Husichen had already seized Heqiao Bridge. Dulü fled west to Leibo Ford and was captured and sent back.

sentences.zh: 椿囚之，送齊神武，斬之都市。

translations.literal: Husichen imprisoned him, sent him to Shenwu of Qi, and he was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Husichen imprisoned him and sent him to Shenwu, who had him beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尒硃天光

translations.literal: Er Zhurong Tiangguang
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong Tiangguang

sentences.zh: 天光，榮從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Tiangguang was the son of Rong's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang was the son of Rong's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 少勇決，榮特親愛之，常預軍戎謀。

translations.literal: From youth he was brave and resolute; Rong especially favored and loved him and regularly included him in military plans.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was brave and resolute. Rong especially favored him and regularly included him in military plans.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，榮據並、肆，仍以天光為都將，總統肆州兵馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaochang era Rong held Bing and Si provinces and still appointed Tiangguang area commander, putting him in overall charge of the troops and horses of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era Rong held Bing and Si provinces and appointed Tiangguang area commander in overall charge of the troops and horses of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，榮向京師，委以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Rong marched toward the capital and entrusted the aftermath to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Rong marched toward the capital and entrusted affairs at home to him.

sentences.zh: 建義初，為肆州刺史，封長安縣公。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Inspector of Sizhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was appointed Inspector of Sizhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an County.

sentences.zh: 榮將討葛榮，留天光在州，鎮其根本。

translations.literal: When Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, he left Tiangguang in the province to guard his base.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, he left Tiangguang in the province to guard his base.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「我身不得至處，非汝無以稱我心。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Where I myself cannot go, no one but you can satisfy my intent.
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Where I myself cannot go, no one but you can satisfy my intent.

sentences.zh: 」永安中，與元天穆東破邢杲。

translations.literal: " In the Yong'an era he joined Yuan Tianmu in the east to defeat Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Yong'an era he joined Yuan Tianmu in the east to defeat Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，天光與天穆會榮於河內。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tiangguang and Tianmu joined Rong at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tiangguang and Tianmu joined Rong at Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮發後，並、肆不安，詔天光兼尚書僕射，為並、肆等九州行台，仍行并州事。

translations.literal: After Rong set out, Bing and Si provinces were unsettled; an edict appointed Tiangguang concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over nine provinces including Bing and Si, while he still administered the affairs of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong set out, Bing and Si provinces were unsettled. An edict appointed Tiangguang concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over nine provinces including Bing and Si, while he still administered the affairs of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天光至并州，部分約勒，所在寧輯。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang reached Bingzhou, he organized and restrained the troops, and wherever he went order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang reached Bingzhou, he organized and restrained the troops, and order was restored wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 顥破，還京師，改封廣宗郡公。

translations.literal: After Hao was defeated, he returned to the capital and his fief was changed to Duke of Guangzong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao was defeated, he returned to the capital and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guangzong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，高平鎮城人赫貴連恩等為逆，共推敕勤酋長胡琛為主，號高平王。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Guilian'en and others of Gaoping Garrison town rebelled and jointly raised the tribal chief Hu Chen of Chiqin as their leader, styling him King of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, He Guilian'en and others of Gaoping Garrison town rebelled and jointly raised the tribal chief Hu Chen of Chiqin as their leader, styling him King of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遙臣沃野鎮賊帥破六韓忉夤。

translations.literal: From afar they submitted to Poliuhan Chouyin, the bandit leader of Woye Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: From afar they submitted to Poliuhan Chouyin, the rebel leader of Woye Garrison.

sentences.zh: 琛入據高平城，遣其大將万俟醜奴來寇涇州。

translations.literal: Chen entered and seized Gaoping city, and sent his great general Moqi Chounu to raid Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen entered and seized Gaoping city and sent his great general Moqi Chounu to raid Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琛後與莫折念生交通，侮僈忉夤。

translations.literal: Later Chen communicated with Moqi Niansheng and treated Chouyin with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chen communicated with Moqi Niansheng and treated Chouyin with contempt.

sentences.zh: 遣使人費律如至高平，誘斬琛，為醜奴所並，與蕭寶夤相拒于安定。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy, Fei Lüru, to Gaoping to lure and behead Chen; he was absorbed by Chounu and faced Xiao Baoyin in opposition at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy, Fei Lüru, to Gaoping to lure and behead Chen. Chounu absorbed Chen's forces and faced Xiao Baoyin in opposition at Anding.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗還。

translations.literal: Baoyin was defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was defeated and retreated.

sentences.zh: 建義元年夏，醜奴擊寶夤於靈州，禽之，遂僭大號。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jianyi, Chounu attacked Baoyin at Lingzhou, captured him, and thereupon usurped the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Jianyi, Chounu attacked Baoyin at Lingzhou, captured him, and usurped the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 時獲西北貢師子，因稱神獸元年，置百官。

translations.literal: At the time he received a tribute lion from the northwest and therefore styled his reign the Divine Beast, first year, and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he received a tribute lion from the northwest and styled his reign the Divine Beast, first year, establishing the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂之，乃除天光使持節、都督、雍州刺史，率大都督武衛將軍賀拔岳、大都督侯莫陳悅等討醜奴。

translations.literal: The court was alarmed and therefore appointed Tiangguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, area commander, and Inspector of Yongzhou, leading Grand General Heba Yue, General of the Martial Guard, and Grand General Houmochen Yue and others to campaign against Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed and appointed Tiangguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, area commander, and Inspector of Yongzhou, leading Grand Generals Heba Yue and Houmochen Yue to campaign against Chounu.

sentences.zh: 天光初行，唯有軍士千人。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang first set out, he had only one thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang first set out, he had only one thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時東雍赤水蜀賊斷路，天光入關擊破之，簡取壯健。

translations.literal: At the time bandits of the Chishui Shu in Eastern Yong blocked the road; Tiangguang entered the pass, defeated them, and selected the strong and fit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits of the Chishui Shu in Eastern Yong blocked the road. Tiangguang entered the pass, defeated them, and selected the strong and fit.

sentences.zh: 至雍，又稅人馬，合得萬疋。

translations.literal: When he reached Yongzhou he also levied men and horses, totaling ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yongzhou he also levied men and horses, totaling ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 以軍人寡少，停留未進。

translations.literal: Because his troops were few, he halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Because his troops were too few, he halted and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 榮遣責之，杖天光百下。

translations.literal: Rong sent a messenger to rebuke him and had Tiangguang beaten one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent a messenger to rebuke him and had Tiangguang beaten one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 榮復遣軍士二千人赴天光。

translations.literal: Rong again sent two thousand soldiers to join Tiangguang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong again sent two thousand soldiers to reinforce Tiangguang.

sentences.zh: 天光令賀拔嶽率千騎先驅，至岐州，禽其行台尉遲菩薩。

translations.literal: Tiangguang ordered Heba Yue to lead one thousand cavalry as vanguard; reaching Qizhou, he captured the mobile headquarters chief Yuchi Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang ordered Heba Yue to lead one thousand cavalry as vanguard. At Qizhou he captured the mobile headquarters chief Yuchi Pusa.

sentences.zh: 醜奴棄岐州走還安定。

translations.literal: Chounu abandoned Qizhou and fled back to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu abandoned Qizhou and fled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 天光發雍至岐，與嶽合勢，破醜奴，獲蕭寶夤。

translations.literal: Tiangguang set out from Yongzhou to Qizhou, joined forces with Yue, defeated Chounu, and captured Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang marched from Yongzhou to Qizhou, joined forces with Yue, defeated Chounu, and captured Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 於是涇、豳、二夏，北至靈州，及賊黨結聚之類，並降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing, Bin, the two Xias, and as far north as Lingzhou, together with bandit groups gathered in clusters, all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jing, Bin, the two Xias, and as far north as Lingzhou, together with scattered rebel bands, all submitted.

sentences.zh: 唯賊行台万俟道洛不下，率眾西依牽屯山，據險自守。

translations.literal: Only the bandit mobile headquarters chief Moqi Daoluo would not submit; he led his troops west to rely on Qiantun Mountain and held the defiles in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Only the rebel mobile headquarters chief Moqi Daoluo refused to submit. He led his troops west to Qiantun Mountain and held the defiles.

sentences.zh: 榮責天光不獲道洛，復遣使杖之百，詔削爵為侯。

translations.literal: Rong rebuked Tiangguang for failing to capture Daoluo, again sent a messenger to beat him one hundred strokes, and an edict reduced his rank from duke to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Rong rebuked Tiangguang for failing to capture Daoluo, had him beaten one hundred strokes again, and an edict reduced his rank from duke to marquis.

sentences.zh: 天光與嶽、悅等復向牽屯討之，道洛戰敗，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Tiangguang with Yue, Yue, and the others again marched against Qiantun to attack him; Daoluo was defeated in battle and fled to Wang Qingyun, the bandit leader of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang with Yue and Houmochen Yue again marched against Qiantun. Daoluo was defeated and fled to Wang Qingyun, the rebel leader of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 慶雲以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，便謂大事可圖，乃自稱皇帝，以道洛為大將軍。

translations.literal: Qingyun, because Daoluo's valor and daring were unmatched, was greatly pleased to gain him and at once judged great affairs achievable; he styled himself emperor and made Daoluo Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun was greatly pleased to gain Daoluo, whose valor was unmatched, and at once judged the great enterprise achievable. He styled himself emperor and made Daoluo Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天光乃入隴，至慶雲所居永洛城，破其東城。

translations.literal: Tiangguang then entered Long and reached Yongluo city where Qingyun resided, breaking its eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang then entered Long and reached Yongluo city where Qingyun resided, breaking its eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 賊遂並趣西城。

translations.literal: The bandits then all rushed toward the western city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then all rushed toward the western city.

sentences.zh: 城中無水，眾聚熱渴。

translations.literal: There was no water in the city; the massed troops suffered from heat and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: There was no water in the city, and the massed troops suffered from heat and thirst.

sentences.zh: 有人走降，言慶雲、道洛欲突出。

translations.literal: Someone fled over to surrender and said that Qingyun and Daoluo intended to break out.
translations.idiomatic: Someone defected and reported that Qingyun and Daoluo intended to break out.

sentences.zh: 天光恐失賊帥，乃遣謂慶雲，可以早降，若水決，當聽諸人今夜共議。

translations.literal: Tiangguang feared losing the bandit leaders and therefore sent word to Qingyun that he could surrender early; if water were released, he would allow everyone to discuss together that night.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang feared losing the rebel leaders and sent word to Qingyun that he could surrender early, and that if water were released he would allow everyone to discuss terms that night.

sentences.zh: 又謂曰：「相知須水，今為小退。

translations.literal: He also said: "Knowing you need water, I will now withdraw a little.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Knowing you need water, I will now withdraw a little.

sentences.zh: 」賊眾安悅，無復走心。

translations.literal: " The bandit host was reassured and pleased and no longer thought of fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebel host was reassured and no longer thought of fleeing.

sentences.zh: 天光密使軍人多作木槍，各長七尺，至昏，布立人馬，為防衛之勢，又伏人槍中。

translations.literal: Tiangguang secretly had many of his soldiers make wooden stakes, each seven feet long; at dusk he deployed men and horses in defensive array and also hid men among the stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang secretly had his soldiers make wooden stakes seven feet long. At dusk he deployed men and horses in defensive array and hid troops among the stakes.

sentences.zh: 其夜，慶雲、道洛果突出，至槍，馬各傷倒。

translations.literal: That night Qingyun and Daoluo indeed broke out; reaching the stakes, the horses were each wounded and fell.
translations.idiomatic: That night Qingyun and Daoluo broke out as expected. Reaching the stakes, their horses were wounded and fell.

sentences.zh: 伏兵便起，同時禽獲。

translations.literal: The hidden troops rose at once and captured them simultaneously.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden troops rose at once and captured them.

sentences.zh: 賊窮，乞降而已。

translations.literal: The bandits were exhausted and merely begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were exhausted and merely begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 天光、嶽、悅等議悉阬之，死者萬七千人，分其家口。

translations.literal: Tiangguang, Yue, Yue, and the others agreed to bury them all alive; seventeen thousand died, and their households were divided up.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang, Yue, and Houmochen Yue agreed to bury them all alive. Seventeen thousand died, and their households were divided up.

sentences.zh: 於是三秦、河、渭、瓜、梁、鄯善咸來款順。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Qins, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Three Qins, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔復天光前官爵。

translations.literal: An edict restored Tiangguang's former offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Tiangguang's former offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 岳聞榮死，還涇州以待，天光亦下隴，與嶽圖入洛之策。

translations.literal: When Yue heard that Rong had died, he returned to Jingzhou to wait; Tiangguang also came down from Long and with Yue plotted a strategy to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue heard that Rong had died, he returned to Jingzhou to wait. Tiangguang also came down from Long and with Yue plotted a strategy to enter Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既而莊帝進天光爵為廣宗王，元曄又以為隴西王。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Zhuang advanced Tiangguang's rank to Prince of Guangzong; Yuan Ye again made him Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Zhuang advanced Tiangguang's rank to Prince of Guangzong. Yuan Ye again made him Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 及聞尒硃兆已入京，天光乃輕騎向都，見世隆等，尋便還雍。

translations.literal: When he heard that Er Zhurong Zhao had already entered the capital, Tiangguang rode with light cavalry toward the capital, saw Shilong and the others, and soon returned to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Er Zhurong Zhao had already entered the capital, Tiangguang rode with light cavalry to the capital, saw Shilong and the others, and soon returned to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 世隆等議廢元曄，更舉親賢，遣告天光。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others deliberated on deposing Yuan Ye and raising a worthy from among the imperial kin, and sent word to Tiangguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and the others deliberated on deposing Yuan Ye and raising a worthy from among the imperial kin, and sent word to Tiangguang.

sentences.zh: 天光與定策，立節閔帝。

translations.literal: Tiangguang joined in fixing the plan and enthroned Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang joined in fixing the plan and enthroned Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 又加開府儀同三司、尚書令、關西大行台。

translations.literal: He was further given Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with the Opening of a Government Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with the Opening of a Government Office, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner with Full Powers over Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 天光北出夏州，遣將討宿勤明達，禽之，送洛。

translations.literal: Tiangguang marched north out of Xizhou, sent a general to campaign against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangguang marched north out of Xizhou, sent a general to campaign against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時費也頭帥紇豆陵伊利、万俟受洛於等據有河西，未有所附。

translations.literal: At the time the Feiyetou chiefs Yidouling Yili and Moqi Shouluoyu and others held Hexi and had not yet attached themselves to any side.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Feiyetou chiefs Yidouling Yili and Moqi Shouluoyu and others held Hexi and had not yet attached themselves to any side.

sentences.zh: 天光以齊神武起兵信都，內懷憂恐，不暇他事。

translations.literal: Tiangguang, because Shenwu of Qi had raised troops at Xindu, harbored worry and fear within and had no leisure for other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shenwu had raised troops at Xindu, Tiangguang harbored worry and fear within and had no leisure for other matters.

sentences.zh: 伊利等，但微遣備之而已。

translations.literal: Toward Yili and the others he merely sent slight preparations against them, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Yili and the others he merely sent slight preparations, and that was all.

sentences.zh: 又除大司馬。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 時神武軍既振，尒硃兆、仲遠等並經敗退。

translations.literal: At the time Shenwu's army had already risen in strength; Er Zhurong Zhao, Zhongyuan, and the others had all been defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shenwu's army had gained strength, and Er Zhurong Zhao, Zhongyuan, and the others had all been defeated and retreated.

sentences.zh: 世隆累使徵天光，天光不從。

translations.literal: Shilong repeatedly sent envoys to summon Tiangguang, but Tiangguang did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong repeatedly sent envoys to summon Tiangguang, but Tiangguang refused.

sentences.zh: 後令斛斯椿苦要天光云：「非王無以能定，豈可坐看宗家之滅？

translations.literal: Later he had Husichen urgently press Tiangguang: "Without Your Highness no one can settle matters—how can you sit and watch the clan's destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Later he had Husichen urgently press Tiangguang: "Without Your Highness no one can settle matters—how can you sit and watch the clan's destruction?

sentences.zh: 」天光不得已，東下，與仲遠等敗于韓陵。

translations.literal: " Tiangguang had no choice; he marched east and with Zhongyuan and the others was defeated at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: " Tiangguang had no choice. He marched east and with Zhongyuan and the others was defeated at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿等先還，於河橋拒之，天光不得度，西北走，被執，與度律並送于神武。

translations.literal: Husichen and the others returned first and blocked him at Heqiao Bridge; Tiangguang could not cross, fled northwest, was seized, and together with Dulü was sent to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Husichen and the others returned first and blocked him at Heqiao Bridge. Tiangguang could not cross, fled northwest, was captured, and together with Dulü was sent to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武送於洛，斬於都市。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent him to Luoyang, and he was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent him to Luoyang, where he was beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尒硃專恣，分裂天下，各據一方，賞罰自出，而天光有定關西之功，差不酷暴，比之兆與仲遠，為不同矣。

translations.literal: The Er Zhurong clan acted with arbitrary power, splitting the realm and each holding a region, granting rewards and punishments on their own authority. Yet Tiangguang had the achievement of pacifying Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent; compared with Zhao and Zhongyuan, he was different.
translations.idiomatic: The Er Zhurong clan ruled with arbitrary power, each holding a region of the divided realm and granting rewards and punishments on their own authority. Yet Tiangguang had pacified Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent than Zhao and Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：魏自宣武之後，政道頗虧。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From the time of Emperor Xuanwu onward, Wei governance was greatly impaired.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: From the time of Emperor Xuanwu onward, Wei governance was greatly impaired.

sentences.zh: 及明皇幼沖，女主南面。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was young and the empress dowager faced south to rule,
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was young and the empress dowager ruled from behind the screen,

sentences.zh: 始則於忠專恣，繼以元叉權重，居官者肆其聚斂，乘勢者極其陵暴，於是四海囂然，已有群飛之漸。

translations.literal: first Yu Zhong acted with arbitrary power, then Yuan Cha held heavy authority; those in office indulged in plunder, those who seized power carried oppression to the extreme—thereupon the four seas were in uproar, and the trend toward mass uprising had already begun.
translations.idiomatic: first Yu Zhong acted with arbitrary power, then Yuan Cha held heavy authority. Officials indulged in plunder and the powerful carried oppression to the extreme. The realm fell into uproar, and the trend toward mass uprising had already begun.

sentences.zh: 逮於靈後反政，宣淫於朝，傾覆之徵，於此至矣。

translations.literal: By the time Empress Dowager Ling resumed rule and flaunted debauchery at court, the signs of collapse had reached their height.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Empress Dowager Ling resumed rule and flaunted debauchery at court, the signs of collapse had reached their height.

sentences.zh: 尒硃榮緣將帥之列，藉部眾之威，屬天下暴虐，人神怨憤。

translations.literal: Er Zhurong rose from the ranks of generals, relying on the prestige of his tribal forces, at a time when tyranny filled the realm and men and spirits alike were filled with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong rose from the ranks of generals, relying on the prestige of his tribal forces, at a time when tyranny filled the realm and men and spirits alike were filled with resentment.

sentences.zh: 遂有匡頹拯弊之志，援主逐惡之功。

translations.literal: He therefore harbored the will to right a tottering state and rescue a failing order, and achieved the merit of supporting the ruler and driving out evil.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore harbored the will to right a tottering state and rescue a failing order, and achieved the merit of supporting the ruler and driving out evil.

sentences.zh: 及夫禽葛榮，誅元顥，戮邢杲，揃韓婁，醜奴、寶夤，咸梟馬市，然則榮之功烈，亦已茂矣。

translations.literal: When he captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, cut down Han Lou, and Chounu and Baoyin—all displayed at Horse Market—then Rong's achievements and glory were indeed abundant.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, cut down Han Lou, and displayed Chounu and Baoyin at Horse Market, Rong's achievements and glory were indeed abundant.

sentences.zh: 而始則希覬非望，睥睨宸極，終乃靈後、少帝，沈流不反。

translations.literal: Yet at first he coveted what was not his due and cast sidelong glances at the imperial throne; in the end Empress Dowager Ling and the Young Emperor were drowned and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first he coveted what was not his due and cast sidelong glances at the imperial throne. In the end Empress Dowager Ling and the Young Emperor were drowned and never returned.

sentences.zh: 河陰之下，衣冠塗地，其所以得罪人神者焉。

translations.literal: Below Heyin, officials and gentry were strewn across the ground—this was how he offended both men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, officials and gentry were strewn across the ground—this was how he offended both men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 至於末跡凶忍，地逼亦已除矣。

translations.literal: As for his final course of cruelty and ruthlessness, his territorial pressure was also removed.
translations.idiomatic: As for his final course of cruelty and ruthlessness, his territorial threat was also removed.

sentences.zh: 而朝無謀難之宰，國乏折沖之將，遂使餘孽相糾，還成嚴敵。

translations.literal: Yet the court had no minister capable of planning against disaster, and the state lacked generals who could repel the enemy at the frontier; thus the surviving remnants joined forces and became a formidable foe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court had no minister capable of planning against disaster, and the state lacked generals who could repel the enemy at the frontier. The surviving remnants joined forces and became a formidable foe.

sentences.zh: 隆實指蹤，兆為戎首，山河失險，莊帝幽崩。

translations.literal: Shilong in fact directed the tracks; Zhao was the ringleader of the host; the mountains and rivers lost their defenses; Emperor Zhuang died in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong directed the operations, Zhao was the ringleader, the mountains and rivers lost their defenses, and Emperor Zhuang died in secret.

sentences.zh: 宗屬分方，作威跋扈，廢帝立主，回天倒日；

translations.literal: The clan kin divided the regions, acted with overbearing arrogance, deposed emperors and raised rulers, turned heaven back and reversed the sun;
translations.idiomatic: The clan kin divided the regions, ruled with overbearing arrogance, deposed emperors and raised rulers, and turned heaven back and reversed the sun;

sentences.zh: 揃剝黎獻，割裂神州，刑賞任心，征伐自己。

translations.literal: they plundered the people, carved up the sacred land, meted out punishments and rewards at whim, and launched campaigns on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: they plundered the people, carved up the sacred land, meted out punishments and rewards at whim, and launched campaigns on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 天下之命，縣于數胡，喪亂弘多，遂至於此。

translations.literal: The fate of the realm hung on a few barbarian chiefs; calamity and disorder were abundant, and matters reached this pass.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the realm hung on a few barbarian chiefs. Calamity and disorder were abundant, and matters reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 豈非天將去之，始以共定；

translations.literal: Was it not that Heaven was about to remove Wei—at first using them to settle matters together;
translations.idiomatic: Was it not that Heaven was about to remove Wei—at first using them to settle matters together;

sentences.zh: 終於惡稔，以至殄滅。

translations.literal: then, when their evil ripened fully, bringing them to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: then, when their evil ripened fully, bringing them to extinction.

sentences.zh: 抑亦魏紓其難，齊以驅除矣。

translations.literal: Thus Wei eased its difficulties, and Qi drove them out and eliminated them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wei eased its difficulties, and Qi drove them out and eliminated them.
